deb_ex.sum: Cites Northern Ireland statistics on under-35 cardiac deaths and urges that more be done to equip the public with CPR and defibrillator skills.

deb_ex.t: Big money donors do not give out of kindness; they pay for access and influence.

deb_ex.t: Does the Minister agree that the way we fund cancer care should also be the way that we fund care of those with dementia?
deb_ex.sum: Notes there have been 23 reviews into social care since 1997 without agreement on funding, and asks whether dementia care should be funded in the same way as cancer care.

deb_ex.t: there is a fundamental unfairness in dementia care being means-tested, while cancer care is funded by us all through general taxation
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Prime Minister to acknowledge the unfairness of means-tested dementia care compared to universally funded cancer care and to address it.

deb_ex.t: I believe that the Treasury should have the power to specify the amount on an annual basis. It is important for the funding of the monarchy to be transparent
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the ability to reduce the grant but calls for annual Treasury-set amounts, greater transparency, and questions about inheritance tax exemptions, the Duchy of Lancaster and freedom of information exclusions.

deb_ex.t: It is clear from this debate that the public have lost trust in politics and the political process, and that is linked to them seeing money have an undue influence on the decisions
deb_ex.sum: Calls for a ban on political donors securing government contracts, citing £60 billion in contracts awarded to party donors over 25 years, and argues wealthy influence must be curbed alongside geographic redistribution of power.

deb_ex.t: it is a disproportionate escalation. Let us not forget that this war was started by the US and Israel choosing to launch attacks on Iran
deb_ex.sum: Criticises both Iran's attacks on shipping and the US escalation, and presses the Minister on what the UK is doing to pressure both parties to return to negotiations.

deb_ex.t: for the past two years we have heard nothing from this Government except excuses. That is simply unacceptable, because we in this country are complicit in what is happening
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the Government's excuses of complexity and need for multilateral action, arguing the legal framework already exists and that partner countries have moved ahead of the UK.

deb_ex.t: If Israeli exporters cannot prove that their exports do not come from illegal settlements, they should not be able to export to us
deb_ex.sum: Argues the burden of proof should fall on Israeli exporters to show goods do not come from settlements, and demands the Minister explain why the Government will not act.

deb_ex.t: On behalf of the Green party, I would like to say how shocked, saddened and horrified I am by Ann Widdecombe’s horrific death—her brutal murder—and my sincere condolences go to her
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the Home Secretary's commitments on security and avoiding speculation, but presses for a specific timescale for action against online polarisation and hatred to protect both those in public life and democracy itself.

deb_ex.t: The climate crisis is upon us. We in the UK are now in the midst of our third heatwave in less than three months. Communities have endured sweltering conditions that have put huge
deb_ex.sum: Opens the debate by linking the climate crisis and heatwaves to the construction sector's carbon footprint, arguing that embodied carbon is a critical gap in UK climate policy that the Government has so far ignored.

deb_ex.t: we need to recognise that we should be reusing buildings as much as possible. We should be reducing the destruction caused by a failure to reuse
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the intervention and argues that regulations requiring whole-life carbon assessment are needed to ensure buildings are reused rather than demolished, applying the waste hierarchy to construction.

deb_ex.t: I could not agree more with the hon. Gentleman. Since I entered this place, I have been campaigning for homes and buildings that are truly fit for the future. We need to take this
deb_ex.sum: Extends her argument that the Government's inaction is creating a fragmented patchwork of local rules that burdens industry, and calls on the Minister to provide national leadership and a clear regulatory pathway aligned with international

deb_ex.t: national regulation on embodied carbon will reduce complexity for the construction industry, not increase it. It will replace fragmentation with consistency
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the use of article 4 to prevent demolition as a last resort and reiterates the case for national regulation to replace the current fragmented local approach, directly challenging the Government's inaction.

deb_ex.t: this is not regulation that industry fears; it is regulation that the construction sector is asking for
deb_ex.sum: Quotes a now-senior minister's own past support for embodied carbon regulation to press the Government to act, and calls for use of the UK net zero carbon buildings standard as a fast-track compliance route.

deb_ex.t: Does she not recognise that Government is the institution that can provide exactly the consistency that the sector requires?
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister to acknowledge that Government is the institution best placed to deliver the consistency that the sector is calling for, challenging the case for further delay.

deb_ex.t: The Minister has outlined the complexities of regulating in this area as in any other area, and I am glad to hear her say that this does not mean the Government will do nothing. Th
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Minister's complexity argument by pointing out that hundreds of industry experts have already created a regulatory framework ready for Government adoption, asking her to acknowledge this preparatory work.

deb_ex.t: Heatwaves, which are becoming more frequent and more severe due to the climate crisis, create a health crisis. We see that in excessive temperatures in our hospitals and other heal
deb_ex.sum: Links the NHS heat crisis to the broader climate emergency, calls on the Minister to support a maximum workplace temperature Bill and push for a government-wide adaptation and resilience plan.

deb_ex.t: What support she plans to provide to local authorities to help them adopt new technologies for tackling potholes and road defects.
deb_ex.sum: Asks what support the government plans to give local authorities to adopt new technologies for tackling potholes and road defects.

deb_ex.t: Why not equip them with cameras and AI-enabled technology, so that they can spot, map and log potholes immediately, as soon as they appear?
deb_ex.sum: Proposes equipping bin lorries with AI cameras to spot and map potholes in real time, urging cross-departmental coordination and funding to roll this out nationally.

deb_ex.t: Will he ban trade in goods, services and investment in both directions immediately, because the facts on the ground are changing now, at pace and faster than ever before?
deb_ex.sum: Criticises the government for more hand-wringing delays and demands an immediate ban on trade in goods, services and investment in both directions, arguing that facts on the ground are changing at pace right now.

deb_ex.t: will he rule out Rosebank and Jackdaw, because the climate damage they would create hugely outweighs any possible benefit
deb_ex.sum: Chowns highlights record heat and harvests as evidence of the climate crisis and presses the Prime Minister to honour his manifesto pledge by ruling out new oil and gas licences including Rosebank and Jackdaw.

deb_ex.t: I would like to speak to amendment 15 and new clause 30, tabled in my name, and to new clauses tabled by other colleagues from across the House. First of all, I welcome the new Min
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes steps in the Bill but argues it must go much further on dirty money, disinformation and structural democratic reform, urging the Minister to encourage the Prime Minister to initiate a national commission on electoral reform.

deb_ex.t: I was speaking in relation to the title of the Bill.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly defends her remarks as relevant to the Bill's title before being ruled out of order again.

deb_ex.t: We have to take big money out of politics, take the poison of disinformation out of politics, and fix our political system once and for all.
deb_ex.sum: Calls for a total ban on corporate donations and annual campaign expenditure limits, arguing big money and disinformation are loopholes the Bill must close completely.

deb_ex.t: the climate damage created by Rosebank and Jackdaw will hugely outweigh any potential economic benefits and therefore rule them out
deb_ex.sum: Argues that climate breakdown already far outweighs any economic benefit from Rosebank and Jackdaw and urges the Minister to rule both fields out entirely.

deb_ex.t: This Bill responds to the widely held view that services for infants, prospective parents and parents of young children are somewhat vulnerable when they rely largely on non-statutory guidance
deb_ex.sum: Introduces his private Member's Bill, explaining its purpose of placing infant and early-years services on a statutory footing and making them accountable to Parliament rather than reliant on non-statutory guidance.

deb_ex.t: This Bill is quite deliberately written at a higher level. It does not specify what the services should be; it empowers Ministers to regulate and make provision for those services.
deb_ex.sum: Walks through the Bill's six clauses, explaining how each places duties on the Secretary of State to define, assess, provide and report on early-years services, and defends the deliberately high-level drafting.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the pressure on off-grid distilleries from rising fuel costs and signals the government is considering temporarily suspending tariffs on kerosene oil.

deb_ex.t: I absolutely wish the hon. Member’s constituents all the best. It is entrepreneurial spirit like that that drives the economy forward. I will give one example of the support: there
deb_ex.sum: Wishes the new owners well and points to extended UK Export Finance as a key government tool to help such businesses diversify and become more resilient.

deb_ex.t: That will give the UK the strongest legal framework on late payments in the G7.
deb_ex.sum: Outlines the Commercial Payments Bill, describing its provisions on payment terms, mandatory interest and enforcement powers as giving the UK the strongest G7 framework on late payments.

deb_ex.t: For too long, large businesses have used small businesses as a source of free credit. That will end under these plans.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Bill will require payment within 60 days with mandatory interest on late invoices, ending the practice of large businesses using small firms as free credit, and promises better cash flow and growth.

deb_ex.t: our small business strategy is improving access to markets for small businesses, improving access to finance for small businesses, and cutting the regulatory burden
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges a tough decade for small businesses and sets out the government's small business strategy covering markets, finance access, and regulatory burden reduction.

deb_ex.t: we have put significant resources into tackling the type of crime she raises. That is becoming a permanent approach under this Government.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the problem of bogus businesses and points to Operation Machinize and ongoing ministerial engagement with Companies House and the Insolvency Service as the government's response.

deb_ex.t: where there is a risk of disruption that does not mean the service will disappear
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the government's commitment to maintaining network size means closures will prompt searches for alternative sub-postmasters rather than permanent loss of service.

deb_ex.t: it was a reminder of the importance of our first employment experiences in making ourselves into fully rounded human beings and workers.
deb_ex.sum: Closes the debate for the Government, celebrating the value of summer jobs from personal experience while defending the Employment Rights Act and challenging Conservative claims about zero-hours contracts.

deb_ex.t: many people value flexibility in the workplace, but some employers have used that flexibility to take advantage of their employees, including young employees.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Employment Rights Act by arguing Conservative Members were defending zero-hours contracts that employers have used to exploit young workers.

deb_ex.t: where people genuinely value that flexibility in the workplace, they will be able to continue to work in that way.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the summer school group and clarifies that the Employment Rights Act does not force seasonal contracts to become permanent, defending Government policy.

deb_ex.t: hundreds of people in his constituency do not have the right to regular hours
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's zero-hours contract reforms by arguing workers who prefer flexibility can keep their arrangements, while those relying on such contracts as their main job deserve income certainty.

deb_ex.t: Maybe he can say why he thinks those hundreds of workers in his constituency should not have the right to full-time employment.
deb_ex.sum: Invites the Conservative Member to explain why workers in his constituency should be denied the right to full-time employment, pressing him to justify opposition to the reforms.

deb_ex.t: Those people will still be able to have those contracts under the legislation, but we are talking about potentially hundreds of people in the right hon. Member’s constituency—that
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's employment and business rates reforms, arguing zero-hours contract changes protect the most vulnerable workers and the youth guarantee package offsets national insurance costs for employers of young people.

deb_ex.t: we are dealing with the issue of youth unemployment by incentivising businesses to employ young people
deb_ex.sum: Defends government policy by emphasising incentives for businesses to hire young people and commits to reducing administrative burdens as part of a net target.

deb_ex.t: This Labour Government will act, and these reforms will deliver the national renewal that our country needs.
deb_ex.sum: Closes the debate defending the government's employment law reforms, business rates changes, and youth unemployment review, dismissing Conservative proposals as outdated.

deb_ex.t: I express regret and apologies, Mr Speaker, not only for the issue you just raised, but that we were not able to lay the regulations before Parliament before they came into force.

deb_ex.t: in the autumn we will, through regulations, appoint an independent valuer to make a judgment on any compensation that is due, and that could be nil.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister confirms British Steel is now publicly owned, outlines plans for a new board, and says an independent valuer will assess any Jingye compensation in the autumn, which could be nil.

deb_ex.t: A key priority for the new board will be looking at ways to reduce costs, and a huge part of that will be investing to help with energy costs.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister agrees that past inaction harmed steelmaking communities and outlines existing energy cost interventions, noting that reducing costs will be a key priority for the new board.

deb_ex.t: Crude production has fallen by 50% over the last 10 years, and we have seen community after community abandoned.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister defends the decision as being in the national interest, not targeted at China, and rejects the Opposition's framing by pointing out that crude steel production fell 50% under the previous Government.

deb_ex.t: As my hon. Friend will be aware, the point of the steel strategy is to do exactly what he describes, which is to ensure that a far greater proportion of UK demand, including for sp
deb_ex.sum: The Minister confirms expanding domestic production of specialist steels is part of the steel strategy and says the new board will address the issue, noting the Government has owned British Steel for only 11 hours.

deb_ex.t: The blast furnaces on the site will continue for some time to come.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister thanks Leigh for his constructive tone, says the key moment for jobs was last year's intervention preventing 2,700 redundancies, and confirms the blast furnaces will continue while the new board modernises the site.

deb_ex.t: This morning, the workers on the site have been briefed on the decision.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister stresses the decision's importance to national security and infrastructure, and confirms workers on site have been briefed this morning with the new board expected to remain closely engaged.

deb_ex.t: the partnership comes with significant resources on the table, through the National Wealth Fund, to help the steel industry become more competitive, particularly on energy efficiency.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister agrees energy costs are central and says the Government is seeking a private-sector partnership backed by National Wealth Fund resources to improve energy efficiency in steel.

deb_ex.t: 80% of the rails we will be travelling on are made by British Steel.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister agrees, noting that 80% of railway rails are made by British Steel, and says public procurement should firmly include British Steel.

deb_ex.t: The blast furnaces at Scunthorpe will be operational for the immediate term.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister reaffirms the steel strategy's preference for electric arc technology as the most competitive future, confirms blast furnaces will remain operational in the near term, and says the new board will address longer-term questions.

deb_ex.t: Without the measures we took, there was a real prospect of our becoming the global dumping ground for uncompetitively subsidised over-production.
deb_ex.sum: The Minister defends the safeguard measures as necessary to prevent the UK becoming a dumping ground, points to transitional arrangements and a 12-month review, and notes ongoing work with the EU on mutual arrangements.

deb_ex.t: As the Minister for Industry has set out, on the issue of cost, it is our intention to continue with the practice under the previous Act of coming to Parliament on a quarterly basi
deb_ex.sum: The Minister commits to quarterly written ministerial statements on costs and says the new board will be accountable to Select Committees.

deb_ex.t: through the work we are doing on public procurement, we are ensuring that there is a clearer line of sight for British steel producers
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms government investment to reduce costs and explains how public procurement guidance will give British Steel a fair chance at infrastructure contracts.

deb_ex.t: the clean industry bonus scheme—for offshore wind, for example—will incentivise its use.
deb_ex.sum: Invites the hon. Member to raise specific regulatory concerns directly and points to revised procurement guidance and the clean industry bonus scheme as mechanisms to support British Steel.

deb_ex.t: I am disappointed in the hon. Gentleman’s lack of faith in my career prospects. I am sure that the Minister for Industry, who has deep expertise in steel and is an excellent Minist
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question with light humour about ministerial continuity but assures the House that the Minister for Industry intends to update Parliament on the new board's strategic objectives.

deb_ex.t: We are deeply committed and open to private sector partnerships to ensure the future of British Steel, and that is an essential and early part of the conversation.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges nationalisation was a reluctant decision, notes the company has only been publicly owned for hours, and reaffirms openness to private sector partnerships for British Steel's future.

deb_ex.t: There are specific arrangements within the trade measures we have taken that are intended to ensure the flow of steel into Northern Ireland
deb_ex.sum: Commits to the suggested meetings with Northern Ireland stakeholders, points to existing trade measure provisions for steel flow into Northern Ireland, and stresses the importance of continued dialogue with the EU.

deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the national security rationale for the treaty, notes the previous Conservative government held 11 rounds of negotiations, and confirms funding will come from existing FCDO and MoD settlements.

deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms unequivocal UK sovereignty over the Falklands and commitment to Falkland Islanders' right to self-determination, stating the UK position is unchanged.

deb_ex.sum: Insists the deal was developed in lockstep with the US, that US endorsement has not been withdrawn, and commits to finding a way forward protecting UK national security.

deb_ex.t: This Government have been absolutely clear that we will ensure there will always be prison cells for people when they are convicted and sentenced to custody.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies there is no specific grooming gangs offence and reaffirms the Government's commitment to ensuring prison cells are always available for those sentenced to custody, contrasting with the Conservatives' prison-building record.

deb_ex.t: I want to ensure that I can look them in the eyes and know that when offenders are convicted and sentenced to custody, there are prison cells for them.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms that the Government always listens to victims but insists prison capacity must be maintained so that convicted offenders can always be imprisoned.

deb_ex.t: grooming has been made a clear aggravating feature. However, I would be happy to meet the hon. Lady to discuss this point if she would find that useful.
deb_ex.sum: Explains that grooming is now an aggravating factor in sentencing but that judges retain discretion over the final sentence, and defends the Government's prison-building record against Conservative criticism.

deb_ex.t: I will ensure that the Under-Secretary of State for Justice, my hon. Friend the Member for Rother Valley (Jake Richards), writes to the hon. Lady.
deb_ex.sum: Commits to ensuring the Prisons Minister writes to the Lib Dem MP with an update on HMP Dartmoor.

deb_ex.t: Conservative Members have talked many times in this debate about how we got here, but they have not been honest about how we got here.
deb_ex.sum: Signals intent to address Conservative Members' account of how the prison crisis arose, implying it has been dishonest.

deb_ex.t: I did work experience with the police as a teenager, back when this country had a Labour Government who were recruiting thousands of additional police officers.
deb_ex.sum: Begins to contrast her own professional experience with the criminal justice system under Labour and Conservative governments to contextualise the prison capacity crisis.

deb_ex.t: That is not a coincidence; it is a choice, repeated by successive Governments for 14 years.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that 14 years of Conservative-led government choices—delayed courts, shuttered courts, reckless probation privatisation—created the prison capacity crisis that necessitates the early release scheme.

deb_ex.t: I am going to continue to make some progress, but I will give way shortly.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly signals she will continue making her case on the origins of the prison crisis before taking further interventions.

deb_ex.t: If prisons run out of space, courts cannot sentence anyone to custody. If courts cannot sentence anyone to custody, they cannot function.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the full scale of Conservative cuts to police, courts, probation and prisons over 14 years, arguing this left prisons at 99% capacity and that without early release the entire justice system risked total breakdown.

deb_ex.t: release does not mean freedom. We are delivering tougher punishment outside prison. We are ramping up tagging to monitor offenders
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the government's early release policy, emphasising public protection measures including tagging, probation funding, and licence conditions, while contrasting the record favourably against the Conservatives.

deb_ex.t: this Government are deporting such offenders in greater numbers than ever before
deb_ex.sum: Minister summarises backbench contributions on criminal justice, defending the government's record on foreign national deportations, court sitting days, and reducing reoffending.

deb_ex.t: I will not give way. A number of hon. Members have spoken passionately about victims, and rightly so. We understand that these issues will be difficult and upsetting for many victi
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends the government's communication with victims through the victim contact scheme, contrasting it with what she describes as chaotic Conservative handling of early releases.

deb_ex.t: Victims were told only days before their offenders were let out, and in some cases they were not told at all.
deb_ex.sum: Minister sets out licence conditions including exclusion zones and a new dedicated helpline for victims, criticising the previous government for informing victims only days before offenders' release.

deb_ex.t: when public bodies fail, the response is candour, not cover-up
deb_ex.sum: Introduces the Bill on Report, describing it as a landmark shift requiring honesty and transparency from public bodies toward bereaved families rather than institutional cover-up.

deb_ex.t: families have had to fight for the truth and their trust in the state to be forthcoming and truthful has been shattered
deb_ex.sum: Credits the Hillsborough families and a wider coalition of campaigners for driving the Bill, stressing it belongs to all families who have fought institutions for the truth.

deb_ex.t: I will make some progress, and then I will take interventions. Many have graciously—often at huge personal and emotional cost—shared their experiences with us to shape the Bill. Th
deb_ex.sum: Thanks campaigners, predecessors and ministers for shaping the Bill, and explains why the Government paused to address Manchester Arena families' concerns about intelligence services.

deb_ex.t: we are clear that the Bill needs to apply across the United Kingdom, and we are working with devolved nations to ensure that happens
deb_ex.sum: Assures the House that the Bill is intended to apply across the whole United Kingdom and that work with devolved nations is ongoing.

deb_ex.t: We are seeking a full culture change, and are trying to prevent any kind of attitude of covering things up
deb_ex.sum: Responds by affirming the Bill seeks a full culture change against cover-ups and offers to meet the hon. Member to discuss the specific Stakeknife case.

deb_ex.t: where information can be disclosed, it should be disclosed, while ensuring that proper protections are in place
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government amendments ensuring compliance directions apply to individual intelligence officers and establishes secure disclosure procedures, while protecting national security.

deb_ex.t: I am very happy to meet the hon. Member and others, specifically in relation to the Ministry of Defence
deb_ex.sum: Offers to meet the hon. Member to discuss how the duty of candour can apply to MoD cases safely.

deb_ex.t: If it is specifically in relation to security services, and to security at the moment—
deb_ex.sum: Begins to conditionally offer to take the intervention, limiting it to security services matters.

deb_ex.t: a public servant does not have to come forward until it is safe to do so, but steps must be taken without delay
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the Bill does not override existing law including the Official Secrets Act, sets out protections for intelligence officers, and announces secondary legislation to extend the duty further.

deb_ex.t: It is absolutely right that recommendations are tracked and that we ensure there is a clear way of giving everyone confidence
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Cabinet Office is working to ensure inquiry recommendations are tracked and offers to brief the hon. Member on progress.

deb_ex.t: The Government have already taken steps to improve transparency in response to inquiry recommendations, including launching the new gov.uk dashboards
deb_ex.sum: Points to new gov.uk dashboards tracking inquiry recommendations and welcomes the Public Administration and Constitutional Affairs Committee's scrutiny work.

deb_ex.t: there is clearly work to be done in relation to inquests and in relation to inquiries and their recommendations
deb_ex.sum: Notes ongoing work by the Chief Coroner on prevention of future deaths reports and acknowledges further work is needed on inquests and inquiry recommendations.

deb_ex.t: the largest expansion of legal aid in a generation, granting access to non-means-tested legal aid to families at any inquest where a public authority is an interested person
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges public confidence in handling recommendations is being actively considered and outlines the legal aid expansion as the largest in a generation to rebalance families against public authority legal teams.

deb_ex.t: we would hope that, in general, one legally aided advocate would be sufficient to support each family through an inquest hearing
deb_ex.sum: Responds to concerns about legal aid advocacy by explaining the expansion, noting one legally aided advocate should generally suffice, but commits to continuing to look at the issue as the Bill progresses.

deb_ex.t: my hon. Friend assists me in finding my place in my notes again, so I thank her
deb_ex.sum: Briefly thanks a colleague for helping her find her place in her notes.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend has been a passionate advocate in relation to legally aided work, and I know that she will take every opportunity to raise concerns about the rates. The amendments m
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges concerns about legal aid rates, sets out Government amendments on archivists, devolved Government provisions and Scottish legal aid, and commits to publishing a clear implementation timeline.

deb_ex.t: The Bill allows a Minister to extend the duty and allows the flexibility to apply it to reviews where it would be most beneficial. I know that my hon. Friend has campaigned long on
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Bill allows Ministers to extend the duty of candour to reviews where beneficial, offers to discuss this further, and pays tribute to bereaved families who campaigned for the legislation.

deb_ex.t: This Bill will finally put that imbalance right. It shifts the system away from secrecy and defensiveness towards openness, honesty and accountability.
deb_ex.sum: Closes the debate as a minister, defending the Government amendments on national security, explaining existing safeguards remain intact, and affirming the Bill will apply to maternity scandals and strengthen accountability across public ins

deb_ex.t: We are clear that we will apply the duty of candour to the Leeds and Sussex maternity reviews.
deb_ex.sum: Responds to specific points on national oversight, maternity reviews, whistleblowing and water companies, confirming the Government's commitments and willingness to work further on outstanding concerns.

deb_ex.t: Restriction zones reverse that burden by confining offenders to specific areas. Will the Justice Secretary be more ambitious about the use of restriction zones
deb_ex.sum: Atkinson welcomes the victims hotline being brought forward and asks the Justice Secretary to be more ambitious in using restriction zones to curtail offenders' freedoms rather than victims'.

deb_ex.sum: Condemns US-Israeli military strikes as illegal and argues the Trump administration is dismantling international law. Warns of catastrophic consequences for ordinary Iranians and calls for diplomacy over force.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms NHS trusts must have business continuity plans for adverse weather and that the Department works closely with NHS England and UKHSA, acknowledging this is an increasingly pressing issue.

deb_ex.sum: Responds by citing the 10-year health plan's prevention focus and a new duty on authorities to consider air quality, and offers to meet the MP.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the programme's progress, noting it finds cancers earlier and narrows outcome gaps, and confirms clear NHS protocols are in place for following up incidental findings.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms that clear national protocols and quality assurance arrangements are in place to ensure incidental findings are reported, followed up and acted on appropriately.

deb_ex.sum: Outlines the national cancer plan's dedicated chapter on children and young people and explains how cancer manuals will set clear quality standards to reduce variation in care.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the forthcoming Select Committee report and commits to responding to it in full.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's commitment to making this the healthiest generation of children, citing investment in family hubs, mental health support, and tobacco legislation.

deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the local initiatives highlighted by the hon. Member and notes they complement government prevention work, including a £1 billion investment in PE and school sport.

deb_ex.sum: Points to the SEND White Paper currently out for discussion as the vehicle through which the government will improve assessment, diagnosis and support for all children with SEND including autism.

deb_ex.t: We are committed to ensuring that no matter where someone is in the country, they have access to the healthcare and support that they need.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the campaign highlighted by the hon. Member, reaffirms the government's commitment to equal healthcare access regardless of location, and agrees to a meeting.

deb_ex.sum: Describes how Sure Start expanded to near-universal provision before being devastated by post-2010 austerity cuts, arguing the Bill is essential to prevent future backsliding.

deb_ex.t: Those savage cuts were truly a tragedy for children everywhere.
deb_ex.sum: Condemns the coalition Government's cuts to Sure Start as a tragedy, quotes Nick Clegg's praise for the programme, and laments the broken pre-election promise to protect it.

deb_ex.t: That is a really good point, which gives us great hope that the Prime Minister will help to rebuild that, and protect what we are discussing, going forward.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly agrees that the Prime Minister's Sure Start record gives hope he will rebuild and protect early years services.

deb_ex.sum: Minister praises the Darren Deady Foundation and accepts the invitation to visit, noting his personal connection as an Afghan veteran.

deb_ex.t: Through Operation Valour, we want to make that support even better, so that every veteran can access the support that they deserve, when they need it.
deb_ex.sum: Minister praises Veterans Contact Point and outlines further Valour progress, including new recognised hubs and the assessment of second-round funding expressions of interest.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Member for her commitment to the veterans in her community, and for raising those important points. Operation Valour does not seek to usurp the wonderful third sec
deb_ex.sum: Minister defends Operation Valour as empowering the third sector rather than replacing it, and attributes housing shortages to the previous Conservative government.

deb_ex.t: I cajoled my two local councils into ceasing that practice by writing to them and lobbying on behalf of veterans.
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges the point and offers to share his own experience of lobbying local councils to stop counting military compensation as income.

deb_ex.t: One veteran rough sleeping is one too many. This Government will always ensure that support is available when needed.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government commitments on veteran homelessness, including £12 million for the reducing veteran homelessness programme and Op Fortitude support services.

deb_ex.t: Op Fortitude has helped more than 1,000 veterans into housing.
deb_ex.sum: Responds by outlining cross-government work with MHCLG and local authorities, exemptions from local connection rules for social housing, and the success of Op Fortitude in housing over 1,000 veterans.

deb_ex.t: the Catterick integrated care centre will open in Richmondshire later this year. This cutting-edge healthcare facility is a joint MOD and NHS initiative, the first of its kind
deb_ex.sum: Announces the forthcoming opening of the Catterick integrated care centre, a joint MOD-NHS facility serving both military and civilian communities in Richmondshire.

deb_ex.t: I would love to visit the facility with him so that we can highlight it as an exemplar that could be transferred to other parts of the country.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the facility should be an exemplar for other parts of the country and offers to visit it with Sunak to promote the model.

deb_ex.t: We are committed to expanding and modernising the five MOD-sponsored cadet forces and to investing to improve opportunities for young people
deb_ex.sum: Minister highlights his personal cadet background and sets out the government's commitment to expanding cadet forces by 30%, with the target to be met by 2035 and an action plan due in October.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Member for raising this issue, but I do not recognise the idea that we have cut the funding. We still intend to expand the cadet forces by 40,000 cadets, and that
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the characterisation that funding has been cut and reaffirms the government's target to expand cadet forces by 40,000 by 2035, directing the hon. Member to the cadet action plan.

deb_ex.t: I would direct her to the cadet action plan, and I will meet her to discuss these issues
deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly to the question about sea cadets, directing the hon. Member to the cadet action plan and offering a personal meeting to discuss the issues.

deb_ex.t: We have invested more than £25 million in Op Courage since the election so that veterans in England can continue to access specialist mental health and wellbeing services.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the government's world-leading blast injury support, £3.65 million scanning technology investment and over £25 million in Op Courage since the election to support veterans' mental health.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for raising such an important question. She is a doughty champion of our servicepeople and we are very grateful for her support. As someone who has four chil
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the pressures of service family life from personal experience and commits to engaging further on the issue, exploring additional support and working with families federations to inform future policy.

deb_ex.t: I will look to take on those ideas and the one that he has raised.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member for the idea and commits to looking at how similar shows of support for veteran communities can be promoted by Ministers across the country.

deb_ex.t: I am aiming to disclose the document to which my hon. Friend referred as soon as possible
deb_ex.sum: Thanks his colleague for championing nuclear testing veterans and commits to disclosing the previously undisclosed fallout report as soon as possible.

deb_ex.t: Did the hon. Member just refer to the nuclear deterrent as “ordinary”?
deb_ex.sum: Queries whether the SNP speaker was describing the nuclear deterrent as merely ordinary.

deb_ex.t: I emphasise that £300 billion is new money; £15 billion is new money
deb_ex.sum: Responds as minister to criticism that there is no new money, asserting that £300 billion and £15 billion are genuinely new investment and attributing current capability gaps to the 2010 spending cuts.

deb_ex.t: The removal of funding specifically in 2010 resulted in the removal of Nimrod and the reduction of our shipyards and boatyards
deb_ex.sum: Attributes current capability risks directly to the 2010 removal of Nimrod and reduction of shipyards under the previous Conservative government.

deb_ex.t: UK defence spending will rise in real terms by 27% between 2023-24 and 2029-30—the largest sustained increase since the cold war
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's programme of defence investment, reform and NATO collaboration, arguing the DIP represents the largest sustained spending increase since the cold war.

deb_ex.t: Britain has always met its NATO spending obligations in the past, and under this Government we always will.
deb_ex.sum: Draws on his military service to affirm backing for the defence investment plan and pledges the government will meet NATO spending obligations, starting with raising defence investment to 2.7% of GDP.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend has advocated for the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank and alternative finance methods for the past two years. It was pleasing to see the DSR Bank announcement
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes his colleague's long-standing advocacy for the DSR Bank and notes recent announcements on the bank and the multilateral defence mechanism, expressing hope the two will be aligned.

deb_ex.t: The DIP will energise the transformation of our armed forces and target resources to reflect how war is waged today.
deb_ex.sum: Argues the DIP will drive transformation through AI, autonomy and uncrewed systems, and defends the autonomous Navy programme as coherent and cost-effective against a critic, citing Portsmouth evidence.

deb_ex.t: at the moment we are providing 150,000 drones a year to Ukraine.
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the timeline will be challenging but says the government must rise to it, listing DIP commitments including a more lethal digital Army, next-generation combat air, an uncrewed systems taskforce and Europe's biggest drone testing sit

deb_ex.t: I thank the right hon. Member for his question. Perhaps we should have a discussion about it outside, because of its ambiguity— [ Interruption. ] The right hon. Member and I will s
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the efficiency-target question and closes by asserting that rapid rearmament is well under way, with investment in new technologies, munitions, factories and jobs and a path to 3% then 3.5% of GDP.

deb_ex.t: our RAF pilots, who have flown thousands of hours and had more than 115 successful engagements
deb_ex.sum: Opens the debate by praising British armed forces serving in the Middle East and outlining the Government's objectives of a diplomatic solution and ceasefire.

deb_ex.t: We say thank you to every member of our military in the middle east, saving lives and working with international partners to defend our interests.
deb_ex.sum: Concludes tribute to British military personnel in the Middle East, expressing national pride in their service.

deb_ex.t: We want to see a diplomatic solution to this crisis. We call for the resumption of a ceasefire and for the United States and Iran to resume negotiations
deb_ex.sum: Defends ministerial attendance, outlines Iranian attacks on shipping and allies, and sets out the Government's unchanged objectives of diplomacy, ceasefire and freedom of navigation.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for his intervention. As I will go on to say, the things we should be concerned about are not limited to the manifestation of kinetic attacks within the regi
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the cyber threat, outlines reinforcement of regional partners' air defences, deployment of HMS Dragon, and warns of economic consequences of conflict in the strait of Hormuz.

deb_ex.t: Our security services tracked more than 20 potentially lethal Iran-backed plots on British soil between October 2024 and October 2025, targeting journalists, dissidents and Jewish people
deb_ex.sum: Explains HMS Dragon's current UK-led role with potential to join a broader French-led mission, and outlines Iran-backed terror plots on British soil and recent sanctions including on HAYI.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for her powerful intervention. It is important to note that that regime does not respect freedom of religion. Back here at home, every one of us, regardless
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that the Iranian regime does not respect freedom of religion and calls on everyone to stand up for others regardless of faith.

deb_ex.t: What a great privilege it is to receive my first intervention from the hon. Gentleman. It is important that he gets a full answer to those questions, and my hon. Friend the Member
deb_ex.sum: Receives the DUP Member's questions graciously and promises fuller answers in closing remarks.

deb_ex.t: any nation that poses such a terror threat abroad, that murders thousands of its own people and brutally suppresses dissent at home, must never acquire a nuclear weapon
deb_ex.sum: Agrees all must be present and contribute to debates on division, and reaffirms that Iran must never acquire a nuclear weapon.

deb_ex.t: nations that are acting within our country to cause division between people and communities and to attack our democracy and our state
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the domestic threat from Iranian state actors seeking to divide communities and attack democracy, and warns of Iran's nuclear stockpile far exceeding JCPOA limits while offering UK assistance in achieving a verifiable deal.

deb_ex.t: to encourage the resumption of negotiations and a ceasefire; to restore freedom of movement in the strait of Hormuz; to deliver the agreements set out in the memorandum of understanding
deb_ex.sum: Closes his opening speech by restating the Government's four core priorities: resuming negotiations, restoring freedom of navigation, delivering the MOU and protecting British people and allies.

deb_ex.t: Will the right hon. Gentleman say why the Conservative Government’s equipment plan had a funding deficit of between £7 billion and £28 billion? It was filled with unfunded programm
deb_ex.sum: Challenges the Opposition's criticism of the DIP by pointing to the previous Conservative government's equipment plan funding deficit and the £298 billion committed under the current plan.

This Government have put Britain back into leadership on international climate change.
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to the questioner's prior work and praises the Government for restoring British leadership on international climate change, highlighting London's role and Imperial College.

deb_ex.t: I agree with my hon. Friend’s comments on public support. Ultimately, pretty much everybody in this House cares about the people and places that we love. This issue comes up time a
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Climate Change Act as a cross-party achievement supported by every Conservative Prime Minister, arguing it represents serious long-term policy and contrasting it with Opposition moves to repeal it.

deb_ex.t: This Government have made more progress on carbon capture and storage than has been made in the last 20 years.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that Peak Cluster is not a Government-backed project and defends the Government's record on carbon capture and storage, inviting further correspondence.

deb_ex.t: I launched a first-of-its-kind taskforce with external experts from security, the military and academia, to boost preparedness for climate change and nature loss.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action including an upcoming energy resilience strategy and a new expert taskforce on climate preparedness and nature loss.

deb_ex.t: The OBR has been incredibly helpful, as have various parts of our financial architecture across the City, which is looking at where the risks are.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the OBR's work on climate economic impacts and points to the new taskforce as part of the government's broader financial resilience approach.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for her contributions on climate change in the debate last week on carbon budget 7. The recent heatwave showed us for the first time the implications that we
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the heatwave's serious impact on schools, hospitals and workplaces and outlines the government's response including the energy resilience strategy, taskforce and cross-government work on updated advice.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend, who contributes to many of these debates. We want to ensure that we have a system that supports reductions in emissions, while also maintaining supply. I do
deb_ex.sum: Responds that the government wants to support emissions reductions while maintaining supply, and expresses continued commitment to Grangemouth's future.

deb_ex.t: we have secured more than £100 billion of private investment
deb_ex.sum: Sets out three government achievements on climate change: carbon budget 7, over £100 billion of private investment secured, and removing systemic friction for energy projects.

deb_ex.t: We have £1 billion of funding for community energy projects, and we are bringing forward more measures to accelerate progress
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates Winchester city council, highlights £1 billion of community energy funding, and signals further measures to accelerate progress on climate, energy bills and energy security.

deb_ex.t: we all have a responsibility for the words and phrases that we use, and a responsibility to tackle misinformation and be honest about the challenges
deb_ex.sum: Thanks her colleague, affirms the need for action at all levels, and calls for responsibility in language and tackling misinformation while acknowledging room for respectful disagreement.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend—another fantastic speaker in the carbon budget debate the week before last—and Ranelagh school students for presenting their ideas. They are not alone; this
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the students, assures them the Government is acting at all levels and announces a new departmental youth scheme.

deb_ex.t: it would not be appropriate for me to comment further on either project
deb_ex.sum: Sets out that the fields are under a live regulatory process and the Secretary of State will decide in due course, while attacking the Conservatives' record on Aberdeen and North sea jobs.

deb_ex.t: As I say, I appreciate that there is a huge amount of interest in the process, but I am sure we can all agree that we want this robust process to take its course. The worst thing t
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's approach of following due process, warning that interference could force the process to be rerun.

deb_ex.t: We are already drilling in the North sea, and we are clear that oil and gas have an important role
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the importance of supporting workers and the supply chain, affirming oil and gas have a role under the Government's pragmatic approach.

deb_ex.t: given the quasi-judicial nature of the process, we cannot get involved further in it
deb_ex.sum: Reiterates the quasi-judicial nature of the process as reason not to comment further, and notes the Prime Minister's announcement of a wildfire summit.

deb_ex.t: we need to take our time with the process, respect its robustness and think about the implications
deb_ex.sum: Thanks her colleague and affirms the Secretary of State will consider all evidence before making a decision.

deb_ex.t: I am very concerned to be respectful of that. I want to ensure, for his constituents and for the rest of the country, that a clear decision is made
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the importance of jobs and the desire for clarity, but says the quasi-judicial process must be respected before a decision can be announced.

deb_ex.t: The Prime Minister has said that we will take a pragmatic approach, and oil and gas will remain part of our future
deb_ex.sum: Repeats the Government's pragmatic position on oil and gas but declines to comment on the specific decisions pending the process.

deb_ex.t: Oil and gas will be part of our energy mix, and the environmental impact assessment that is taking place will take account of Scope 3 emissions
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges oil and gas will remain in the energy mix and confirms Scope 3 emissions will be part of the environmental impact assessment.

deb_ex.t: reducing venting and flaring would represent a cost and efficiency saving. We should be using our energy efficiently
deb_ex.sum: Agrees methane reduction is important for efficiency and the environment, and says she is working domestically and internationally to address venting and flaring.

deb_ex.t: Scope 3 emissions will be part of the environmental impact assessment, which will be given to the Secretary of State and will feed into her decision-making process
deb_ex.sum: Offers to review the BBC report and confirms Scope 3 emissions will be included in the environmental impact assessment informing the Secretary of State's decision.

deb_ex.t: we have expanded the North sea jobs service to support workers. He is right that there is a huge crossover between renewables and oil and gas workers
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the Government's expanded North sea jobs service and agrees the Secretary of State will factor in the crossover between oil and gas and renewables workers.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Lady for her question. I admire her trying to lure me into a conversation on independence and devolution. I am afraid that that is not part of the scope of the dis
deb_ex.sum: Declines to be drawn on devolution or a specific timeline, prioritising the robustness of the process and reaffirming commitment to a just transition for Scottish workers.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for his excellent analysis of why we have ended up here; he is absolutely right. It is on all of us to respect the process. I think that the feeling of the H
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the previous speaker's analysis blaming the Conservatives and defends the need for a robust process before announcing a decision.

deb_ex.t: we also need to make sure that we have other sources of energy. That is why record investment in clean energy has been secured
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the declining basin argument but pivots to highlight government investment in clean energy as the broader solution.

deb_ex.t: we are, at the moment, a price-taker on the international fossil fuel markets, which has an impact on our constituents
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that fossil fuel price volatility harms constituents and highlights the Secretary of State's focus on energy affordability as the Government's response.

deb_ex.t: I thank the hon. Lady for her question and for her passion on this topic. The environmental impact assessment that has been part of the process will take account of Scope 3 emissio
deb_ex.sum: Notes that the environmental impact assessment includes Scope 3 emissions and signals the Government's serious commitment to climate change without pre-empting the decision.

deb_ex.t: we know that climate change is a key issue. We saw the wildfires this summer and, only this week, we saw the Prime Minister talking in his first interventions
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms that process robustness must be respected and that climate change is a central concern, citing the Prime Minister's COP commitment.

deb_ex.t: it was only in August that these consultations closed. There is a lot of interest in this place and outside, and our Secretary of State wants to consider things properly
deb_ex.sum: Defends the pace of decision-making by noting consultations only closed in August and insists proper process is needed to avoid further legal challenges.

deb_ex.t: I cannot make any further comments on these particular projects because of the robust regulatory process that is under way
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the Member for his views but declines to comment further on the specific projects given the ongoing regulatory process.

deb_ex.t: nobody would say that this Government have not moved at pace in terms of our clean energy mission
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the charge of slow decision-making, noting the consultation only closed in August, and highlights the Government's overall pace on the clean energy mission.

deb_ex.t: I appreciate the strength of feeling—I can hear the strength of feeling on both sides of this House
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the strength of feeling on both sides but declines to comment further on the specific decisions, reaffirming the Government's commitment to an efficient energy system.

deb_ex.t: Getting into any defence of specific areas may lead me to potentially say things that I should not say as it is a decision for the Secretary of State
deb_ex.sum: Declines to defend or challenge any specific element of the Rosebank case and notes the Secretary of State will consider the full environmental impact assessment.

deb_ex.t: I note my hon. Friend’s opinion. As I say, there is a strength of feeling on the different sides of the House. We are noting that, but I will make no comment. On her question about
deb_ex.sum: Notes the range of views without pre-empting the decision and condemns the Conservative suggestion to repeal the Climate Change Act as baffling.

deb_ex.t: The Secretary of State has put energy affordability at the heart of our agenda, and we will continue to do that
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Secretary of State's long-standing commitment to tackling fuel poverty and the Government's record investment in warm homes as the answer to energy affordability concerns.

deb_ex.t: we are very much in favour of evidence-based policymaking
deb_ex.sum: Minister briefly reassures the House that the government is committed to evidence-based policymaking on the fields.

deb_ex.t: the robustness of this process is key. We need to ensure that we respect the process, which will lead to clarity on the decision
deb_ex.sum: Minister welcomes the suggestion about scrutiny and emphasises that the robustness of the process will lead to clarity on the final decision.

deb_ex.t: the Secretary of State will make a decision in due course, taking account of the new evidence that she has received
deb_ex.sum: Minister acknowledges the North Sea's wide impacts on jobs, investment and communities and confirms the Secretary of State will make a decision in due course based on new evidence.

deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's decision not to divide on the Opposition day motion, warns that halting the Sentencing Act would recreate the prison capacity crisis, and reiterates commitment to balancing safety with sustainability.

deb_ex.t: the Opposition party has no plan for how to deal with the prison crisis that its amendment would have brought about later this year
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the Opposition's cross-party offer as hollow given they have no credible plan for prison capacity, and pledges that by the end of this Parliament more criminals will be behind bars than ever under Labour.

deb_ex.t: We are ramping up tagging to monitor offenders in the community, with thousands more subject to 24/7 monitoring and curfews
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's community supervision toolkit—restriction zones, tagging, licence conditions and a £100 million tagging expansion—and defends the probation investment as the alternative to system collapse.

deb_ex.t: either strict licence conditions in the community for those who have already served time in prison under the changes; or, simply put, the collapse of the system altogether
deb_ex.sum: Argues that the choice is between managed licence conditions for those who have already served time or total system collapse, and highlights new victim rights under the Victims and Courts Act 2026.

deb_ex.t: Every offender has a level of dangerousness, which is risk-assessed by probation as and when they leave prison
deb_ex.sum: States that dangerousness is already assessed by judges and probation for every offender and closes by defending the government's prison-building and sentencing reform programme.

deb_ex.t: The Foreign Secretary and I have discussed many of these questions, and he will of course be discussing Ukraine. We have made a signal contribution to European security through our
deb_ex.sum: Confirms Ukraine will be a top priority in the Foreign Secretary's discussions but does not commit specifically to supporting the asset-seizure initiative.

deb_ex.t: I can reassure my hon. Friend’s constituents that, after many years of neglect, we are getting back to the table: I was at the table yesterday and the Foreign Secretary will be at
deb_ex.sum: Reassures that the government is actively re-engaging with the EU on steel, youth opportunities and R&D, and will push ahead in coming weeks.

deb_ex.t: Are we ambitious to go further and faster? Yes, we are. I said that in Europe yesterday and we have said it repeatedly.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the lack of a summit date as standard diplomatic practice and reaffirms the government's ambition to go further and faster on UK-EU partnership.

deb_ex.t: To help more Members get in, questions need to be short and limited to just one question.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker asks Members to keep questions short and limited to one question to allow more contributions.

deb_ex.t: The questions are far too long. Too many colleagues will be disappointed unless questions are kept short
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker intervenes to remind Members to keep questions short so that more colleagues can speak.

deb_ex.t: Order. Gosh—a long question and the hon. Member is saying “you”; it is not my responsibility. Minister, over to you.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker intervenes again to note the question was too long and that responsibility lies with the Minister, not the chair.

deb_ex.t: What can I do to restore confidence, or what can the Minister do? You mean the Minister?
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker corrects the member's use of 'you' in addressing the Minister, clarifying it is the Minister's responsibility not the Chair's.

deb_ex.t: nothing in the Lords amendments engages Commons financial privilege
deb_ex.sum: Confirms no financial privilege is engaged by the Lords amendments, a procedural ruling as Deputy Speaker.

deb_ex.t: With this it will be convenient to discuss Lords amendments 2 to 6
deb_ex.sum: Notes it is convenient to discuss Lords amendments 2 to 6 alongside amendment 1.

deb_ex.t: normally when a Member is called last, they are under a time limit, but you now have more than an hour
deb_ex.sum: Makes a procedural remark noting the next speaker has substantial time available.

deb_ex.t: I call the Minister to wind up
deb_ex.sum: Procedural remark inviting the Minister to wind up the debate.

deb_ex.t: Before the Minister responds, let me say that one question is enough.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker intervenes procedurally to remind the previous speaker that one question is sufficient before the Minister responds.

deb_ex.t: Order. I know that this is a very sensitive debate, but we do not use “you” and “yours”.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker intervenes to remind the shadow minister not to use the word 'you' when addressing the Minister, in line with parliamentary convention.

deb_ex.t: It is clear that the Minister is not giving way just now; she may choose to do so in a moment.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker reminds the House that the Minister is not giving way and Members should wait until she chooses to do so.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Member, who has been here longer than I have, fully understands that I am not responsible for the content of the Minister’s speech. The Minister may comment, if she
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker responds that the content of the Minister's speech is not a matter for the Chair.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member has most definitely put his point on the record, but it is not a matter for the Chair.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker notes the point is on the record but rules it is not a matter for the Chair, directing the Member to the Table Office.

deb_ex.t: it is easier to see a doctor here than to get a GP appointment
deb_ex.sum: Makes a wry aside noting it is easier to see a doctor in the Commons chamber than to get a GP appointment, implicitly probing NHS access pressures.

deb_ex.t: I call James Naish to make the final Back-Bench contribution.
deb_ex.sum: Calls the next speaker to make the final Back-Bench contribution; purely procedural.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Minister for giving notice of his point of order, and for seeking to correct the record so quickly, which he has now done.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker thanks the Minister for promptly correcting the record and considers the matter resolved.

deb_ex.t: Unless I am misunderstanding him, the Minister has committed to making a policy announcement this month. There are only a few more sitting days, and he will know that Mr Speaker do
deb_ex.sum: Presses the Minister on whether a policy announcement has been committed to this month and reminds him that announcements must be made to the House first for proper scrutiny.

deb_ex.t: The speaking limit will drop to three minutes after the next speaker.
deb_ex.sum: Chair announces that the speaking limit will drop to three minutes after the next speaker.

deb_ex.t: Back Benchers are on a four-minute speaking limit. We have found some more time.
deb_ex.sum: Chair corrects the earlier announcement, confirming that Back Benchers have a four-minute speaking limit as more time has been found.

deb_ex.t: I will now announce the results of today’s deferred Divisions. On the draft Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 (Establishment of Schools) (Consequential Amendments) Regulati
deb_ex.sum: Chair announces the results of three deferred Divisions, confirming that the Ayes have it in each case.

deb_ex.t: I am going to squeeze in one more speaker, with two minutes.
deb_ex.sum: Chair announces she will call one more brief speaker before moving to front benchers.

deb_ex.t: Unfortunately, I have to go to the Front Benchers now. I call the shadow Minister.
deb_ex.sum: Chair closes the Back-Bench debate and calls the shadow Minister.

deb_ex.t: With the leave of the House, I will group motions 5 to 10 together.
deb_ex.sum: Groups and puts multiple statutory instrument motions forthwith, reporting the outcomes including two deferred divisions and approved appointments to IPSA and the Electoral Commission.

deb_ex.t: We do not talk about colleagues by their first and second names. We mention their constituencies
deb_ex.sum: Madam Deputy Speaker corrects the hon. Member for referring to a colleague by their full name rather than by constituency, reminding the House of the correct convention.

deb_ex.t: I am not going to get everybody in, and interventions are not helping.
deb_ex.sum: As Chair, reminds the House that interventions are preventing all Members from being called and that she has already informed the Whips of this.

deb_ex.t: This new clause provides for an exemption from the duty of candour and assistance for bodies such as the National Archives
deb_ex.sum: Reads the new clause providing an exemption from the duty of candour for bodies like the National Archives in respect of their statutory records-holding responsibilities.

deb_ex.t: New clause 2— Offence of wilfully destroying information or records relevant to an inquiry or investigation
deb_ex.sum: Outlines the full suite of new clauses and amendments to be debated, covering post-legislative assessment, destruction of records offences, compliance monitoring, and related matters.

deb_ex.t: interventions must be short and to the point. Lots of colleagues want to get in on the debate
deb_ex.sum: Calls for brevity in interventions so that more Members can contribute to the debate.

deb_ex.t: Minister, either you take an intervention or do not. Please do not continue a conversation when Members are seated.
deb_ex.sum: Calls the Minister to order, instructing her to either take or decline the intervention rather than conduct a side conversation.

deb_ex.t: many colleagues wish to contribute to the debate, so I hope she is coming to her conclusion soon
deb_ex.sum: As Deputy Speaker, reminds the Minister that many colleagues wish to contribute and asks her to conclude soon.

deb_ex.t: It would be remiss of me if I did not put on record my thanks to Godfrey and Margaret—my Nigerian mum here—in the Tea Room.
deb_ex.sum: Uses a point of order to add personal thanks to the Tea Room staff who are retiring.

deb_ex.t: Mr Sewards, you have left many minutes on the clock for a change.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker briefly and light-heartedly notes that the speaker has left many minutes on the clock.

deb_ex.t: I call Mark Sewards for the final Back-Bench contribution—not on a five-minute speaking limit but with 60 minutes of debate left.
deb_ex.sum: Acts in procedural capacity as Deputy Speaker, inviting the final Back-Bench speaker and noting the remaining debate time.

deb_ex.t: I will call Members to ask questions on the subject of the statement—these should be brief questions, not full speeches.
deb_ex.sum: Chair announces the Select Committee statement procedure, setting out rules for questions and interventions.

deb_ex.t: There was no bobbing earlier. Does the Member really intend to contribute?
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker queries whether a Member who had not bobbed genuinely wishes to contribute.

deb_ex.t: Many Back Benchers wish to speak, so I suspect that there will be a speaking limit.
deb_ex.sum: Announces the Sir David Amess summer Adjournment debate, calls the first speaker and notes a likely speaking limit.

deb_ex.t: Order. There will be a four-minute speaking limit for Back-Bench Members. I want to put on the record my gratitude to the late Sir David Amess. He was a huge mentor of mine and he
deb_ex.sum: Sets a four-minute speaking limit, pays personal tribute to Sir David Amess and thanks her constituency team.

deb_ex.t: A reminder for colleagues that we do not mention Members’ names directly; we mention them by their constituencies.
deb_ex.sum: Reminds Members of the House rule against referring to other Members by name.

deb_ex.t: In keeping with the late David Amess’s approach, the summer Adjournment debate is indeed broad.
deb_ex.sum: Notes that the broad range of topics raised is in keeping with the spirit of the Sir David Amess debate.

deb_ex.t: questions need to be super short. Let us keep the responses tight as well, Prime Minister.
deb_ex.sum: Deputy Speaker intervenes to remind members to keep questions and responses brief.

deb_ex.t: In order to help me to get every Member in, questions must be just one sentence
deb_ex.sum: Acts as Deputy Speaker, calling the next speaker and requesting one-sentence questions to allow all Members to contribute.

deb_ex.t: Members should avoid wider speculation that could be prejudicial in any future criminal trials.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out procedural guidance from the Chair on sub judice rules for the debate, granting a waiver for discussion of support and wider issues while urging Members not to discuss case details, motives, or guilt.

deb_ex.t: we have been in the Chamber a long time, and we have other items of business to get to, so please keep questions short and answers just as short
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker intervenes to remind Members to keep questions and answers short given the length of the session and other business pending.

deb_ex.t: I am reluctant even to mention this, because all the Members here are so highly experienced, but when mentioning another Member in the Chamber, the etiquette is to give them prior
deb_ex.sum: Reminds Members of the convention of giving prior notice before mentioning another Member in the Chamber, noting the relevant Member is absent.

deb_ex.t: I will extend the time limit because we have gathered some time.
deb_ex.sum: The Deputy Speaker extends the speaking time limit and calls the next speaker.

deb_ex.t: this business has to conclude by 8.3 pm, and that the shadow Front-Bench team may wish to speak on it
deb_ex.sum: Reminds the House of the time limit for the business and notes the shadow Front Bench may wish to speak.

deb_ex.t: I am not responsible for the content of speeches of Members, Secretaries of States or shadow Secretaries of State.
deb_ex.sum: Responds to the point of order by explaining the Chair is not responsible for Members' speech content and invites the shadow Secretary of State to respond briefly.

deb_ex.t: both points have been put on the record. I will leave it there.
deb_ex.sum: Closes the exchange, noting both points are on the record and declining to prolong the matter further.

deb_ex.t: With leave of the House I will group motions 3 to 6 together.
deb_ex.sum: Groups and moves approval of four draft statutory instruments covering births and deaths registration, energy prices, international development, and armed forces service complaints.

deb_ex.t: Let us speed up business questions a little bit, so everybody can get in.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly urges Members to keep contributions concise so all can participate.

Bus services are vital for connecting communities to jobs, education and essential services. We have confirmed over £3 billion for buses over the next three years, including provid
This Government believe in better buses across the UK, and half of the £1.4 billion local authority bus grant resource funding is going to support services in mayoral strategic aut

Illegal e-bikes have no place on our roads. My Department has published guidance to make it clear that e-bikes that exceed the legal power and speed limits are treated as motor veh
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position that illegal e-bikes must be registered and insured and that sellers of conversion kits must inform consumers of the legal implications.

deb_ex.t: The Department for Business and Trade has consulted on new product safety regulations and sought views on the targeted regulation of some products, including e-bike batteries and conversion kits.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the hon. Member's advocacy and confirms DBT has consulted on regulating e-bike batteries and conversion kits, with a response expected in the autumn.

deb_ex.t: We have legislated to introduce numerous lane rental schemes and are devolving powers to establish future schemes to mayors.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out government action on congestion, including lane rental schemes and devolved powers to mayors to enable local decision making.

deb_ex.t: I am sorry to hear about the issues facing my hon. Friend’s constituents; I know how much he does to promote their interests. This Government are investing record sums in road main
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the constituent issues raised, highlights record government investment in road maintenance and tougher rules on street works, and directs the member to press Essex county council.

deb_ex.t: I am sure that the Roads and Buses Minister would be happy to continue those discussions.
deb_ex.sum: Notes previous meetings with the hon. Member about road disruption in his constituency and offers further discussions with the Roads and Buses Minister.

deb_ex.t: National Highways is considering in detail with local partners the case for detrunking the A69 and trunking the A689.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges safety incidents on the A69 and confirms National Highways is working with local partners on the case for detrunking, promising an update in due course.

deb_ex.t: The Government are committed to improving transport connectivity across the country. Through the £2.3 billion local transport grant, Staffordshire will receive more than £96 millio
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the £2.3 billion local transport grant and Staffordshire's £96 million share, and agrees to meet the hon. Member to discuss local transport priorities.

deb_ex.t: I would, of course, be very happy to meet them to talk about what we can do to improve safety on that road
deb_ex.sum: Extends sympathies to the family and agrees to meet the MP and constituents to discuss improving safety on that road.

deb_ex.t: we have said in the cycling and walking investment strategy that we intend to legislate for them in future.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government's intention to legislate for side road zebra crossings as part of the cycling and walking investment strategy.

deb_ex.t: New powers in the Crime and Policing Act 2026 mean that the police can seize e-bikes classed as motor vehicles when they are being used antisocially
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern about illegal e-bikes and highlights new police powers under the Crime and Policing Act 2026 to seize them when used antisocially.

deb_ex.t: My Department has commissioned specific research into those issues so that we can better plan action to tackle that.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern about illegal e-bikes in the gig economy and confirms the Department has commissioned specific research to plan action.

This Government are committed to delivering a truly national civil service, one that lives and breathes the communities that we represent across the UK. We have exceeded our target
I congratulate my hon. Friend the Member for Camborne and Redruth (Perran Moon) on securing this debate and on his tireless work on behalf of Cornwall and its residents. I will als
I am grateful to the hon. Member for South Devon (Caroline Voaden) for securing this important debate. I start by saying that the Government absolutely understand and sympathise wi
