We have been very clear that Royal Mail’s service is unacceptable, and we will continue to say that as long as it is unacceptable. The public expect a well-run postal service, with
deb_ex.sum: Agrees Royal Mail's service is unacceptable, notes Ofcom fines and a Business and Trade Committee inquiry, and urges Royal Mail to improve its service for all constituents.

deb_ex.t: We have introduced the Great British summer savings scheme to help people enjoy a day out for less.
deb_ex.sum: Wishes the MP a happy birthday, thanks community support providers, and highlights the Government's Great British summer savings scheme to help families with summer costs.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman is absolutely right to raise the issue of the importance of parks. I am certain that Baysgarth and Bridge View parks are lovely places, and that their awards are
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates the award-winning parks and highlights the Government's Pride in Place programme providing up to £5.8 billion to support towns and empower local communities.

deb_ex.t: ignoring requests for meetings is simply unacceptable.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that ignoring meeting requests is unacceptable and urges Trinity Estates to engage in good faith to resolve the matter for the MP and his constituents.

deb_ex.t: acting and doing more to tackle cancer, which this Government are absolutely committed to doing, is of such importance to local people and communities.
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to all involved in the cancer centre appeal, expresses hope the council will act promptly, and reaffirms the Government's commitment to tackling cancer.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is a fantastic champion for her local community. I will ensure that the Minister overseeing the scheme hears what she has said, and we will get her an update on how
deb_ex.sum: Praises the MP as a champion for her community and promises to ensure the relevant Minister hears her request and provides an update on accessing the playground funding scheme.

deb_ex.t: It is vital that young people learn about where their food comes from.
deb_ex.sum: Encourages the MP to seek a debate after recess and shares his own experience of a primary school outdoor education programme, endorsing the value of young people learning about food and the outdoors.

deb_ex.t: The DVLA has recruited more staff to the drivers medical casework team and its contact centre to deal with the sustained increase in the volume and complexity of applications, but
deb_ex.sum: Notes the DVLA has recruited more staff to handle increased applications, acknowledges constituent frustration, and recommends the MP seek a Westminster Hall debate in September.

deb_ex.t: It is important that we get a fair system, but it is also important that we have an effective and efficient system that puts people at the centre.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the distress caused to the family and community, affirms the need for a fair and efficient system, and offers to take up the case with the Home Office.

deb_ex.t: if they do not, my hon. Friend will continue to raise the issue until they do.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights Government investment of £582 million to support local authorities on air quality, expresses disappointment at the situation, and warns the company and agencies the MP will persist until action is taken.

deb_ex.t: The new places of worship renewal fund is open for applications, but, as the hon. Gentleman knows, it is an England-only fund administered by Historic England. It is for the Scotti
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies the fund is England-only and administered by Historic England, places responsibility on the Scottish Government to act, and notes they have received the biggest devolution settlement to date.

deb_ex.t: this week we have brought forward our plan for music, detailing our ambition to provide people in every corner of the country with the opportunity
deb_ex.sum: Praises Hardwicke Circus and endorses the Government's new music plan aimed at giving people across the country equal opportunity to build careers in music.

deb_ex.t: There should not be a postcode lottery in this area, or indeed in any other area.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the importance of prevention and agrees there should be no postcode lottery, directing the member to apply for a Westminster Hall or Adjournment debate.

deb_ex.t: Taking part in public life is an honour and a privilege, and we should encourage everyone who aspires to public service to be able to follow that ambition.
deb_ex.sum: Encourages the summer school participants and affirms the value of public service, supporting the goal of broadening access to political participation.

deb_ex.t: the Government are determined to put that right; we are taking action and investing.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges dental access and coastal community challenges, asserts the Government is taking action on dental services, and promises to seek an update from the Minister on the Whitty report.

deb_ex.t: care providers must employ fit and proper staff. I understand that the provider he mentions has been placed in special measures to ensure it makes significant improvements.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the provider has been placed in special measures and signals support for CQC enforcement powers being used to address inadequacies.

deb_ex.t: the Chancellor has delivered the highest growth in the G7; I see that the most recent numbers confirm that is happening.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's economic record citing highest G7 growth and falling inflation, while accepting that the incoming Administration should address Parliament on its plans.

deb_ex.t: It is unacceptable that women face long waits for the health services they need. We published our renewed women’s health strategy to deliver women’s health priorities. We are commi
deb_ex.sum: Calls long waits for women's health services unacceptable, cites the renewed women's health strategy, and encourages the member to apply for a Westminster Hall or Adjournment debate.

deb_ex.t: The next Prime Minister has made clear the importance that he attaches to reindustrialisation, particularly in communities that, for a number of reasons, have felt left behind.
deb_ex.sum: Endorses reindustrialisation as a priority for the incoming Prime Minister and suggests a Westminster Hall or Adjournment debate for an early ministerial update.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Gentleman will appreciate that a new Administration will want to look across some of the commitments that have been made to see whether they want to take them forwar
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges mixed views on the visitor levy and indicates the new Administration will review commitments, promising debate opportunity after recess.

deb_ex.t: I join my hon. Friend in paying tribute to Gerry Borge and all the members of the Lisbon Maru Memorial Association for their work in honouring the memory of those affected by this
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to the Lisbon Maru Memorial Association and emphasises the importance of honouring the more than 800 allied prisoners of war who died.

deb_ex.t: common ridings are an important tradition, bringing communities together, preserving local history and putting on a spectacular display for visitors.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the member for the invitation and praises common ridings as an important tradition that brings communities together and attracts visitors.

deb_ex.t: the Government have been instrumental in bringing forward advanced industrial rights for working people; it is therefore sad to learn of what is taking place in her constituency.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the Government's employment rights record and suggests an Adjournment debate to explore further measures, expressing hope the dispute will be resolved.

deb_ex.t: If she wants a meeting with an Education Minister to talk about what might happen in the legislative process, I will help her to achieve that.
deb_ex.sum: Praises young carers and the hon. Lady's advocacy, and offers to facilitate a meeting with an Education Minister to discuss legislative options.

deb_ex.t: It is unacceptable that people face delays due to medical conditions. We recognise that such delays have knock-on consequences.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the unacceptable delays and notes the DVLA's new casework system, promising to raise the matter with the relevant Minister and consider a statement on return.

deb_ex.t: we want not only to clean up local communities, but to put in their hands the powers to do so.
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the Government's commitment to empowering local communities to clean up and suggests the hon. Lady pursue a Backbench Business or Westminster Hall debate.

deb_ex.t: I commend the McKellen pupils at St Philip Westbrook primary school for their thoughtfulness on these matters.
deb_ex.sum: Commends the pupils and points to the national homelessness plan and Vagrancy Act repeal, suggesting a Westminster Hall or Adjournment debate for a ministerial response.

deb_ex.t: small businesses are the heart of our local communities—that is a constant theme running through Government policy.
deb_ex.sum: Congratulates the award winners, agrees small businesses are central to Government policy, and suggests an Adjournment debate for a ministerial response.

deb_ex.t: Reform offers a great deal in order to get elected and then delivers very little when elected.
deb_ex.sum: Backs the hon. Member's campaign, criticises Reform's record in office, and expresses hope the council reverses its decision.

deb_ex.t: As the hon. Lady suggests, the next Prime Minister was absolutely central to helping to deliver the Public Office (Accountability) Bill. It is crucial that we got that Bill through
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the Bill is just a first step and that changing institutional culture is crucial, expressing confidence the incoming Prime Minister will continue to press the issue.

deb_ex.t: The service provided by Capita has been, quite frankly, dreadful. Too many pension scheme members still face unacceptable delays after years of dedicated public service.
deb_ex.sum: Condemns Capita's service as dreadful, promises to raise individual cases with relevant Departments, and commits to an update to the House in September.

deb_ex.t: we have invested around £100 million for the biggest upgrade of national resilience capabilities in nearly 20 years, to combat the escalating threat of wildfires.
deb_ex.sum: Praises the fire service, raises the hon. Member's concerns with Ministers, and cites £100 million invested in national resilience capabilities and £2 billion for fire authorities.

deb_ex.t: infrastructure needs to be built alongside those new homes. Our planning frameworks are clear that large-scale development should be sustainable and infrastructure-led.
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the 1.5 million homes target and insists planning frameworks require sustainable, infrastructure-led development, recommending a Westminster Hall or Adjournment debate.

deb_ex.sum: Thanks disability organisations for their support and gives assurance that the final report will be properly co-produced, with broad engagement after the summer.

deb_ex.sum: Notes the strong response to the call for evidence and commits to removing the hostile and adversarial characteristics of the current application process.

deb_ex.sum: Confirms the DLA-to-PIP transfer age proposal is under consideration following the Green Paper consultation and pledges cross-government working.

deb_ex.sum: Outlines how completing the co-production review and allowing people to observe the new system in practice will rebuild trust among both disabled people and taxpayers.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that greater personalisation is worth exploring, noting the current system is quite lumpy with few rates.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the issue and points to work through the Crime and Policing Act 2026 and the VAWG strategy as vehicles for addressing intimate image abuse.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's plan for a reformed, human rights-compliant Legacy Commission with veteran safeguards and Irish information sharing.

deb_ex.sum: Reassures the House that the new Defence Secretary remains committed to the Bill and that the amendments will be brought forward shortly.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend makes an important point about this piece of legislation. As we know, the Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy and Reconciliation) Act 2023 did not command support acro
deb_ex.sum: Defends the need to repeal and replace the 2023 Act, which lacked cross-community support, and expresses confidence the new Bill will be fair and balanced.

deb_ex.t: When people see those amendments, they will realise that they are fair and reasonable with regard to the protection of our veterans.
deb_ex.sum: Disagrees with the former minister's assessment and argues the amendments will provide fair, reasonable and first-ever statutory protections for veterans.

deb_ex.t: I do not accept that, because all the Northern Ireland political parties were opposed to the immunity that was at the heart of the 2023 legacy Act. It had no support from political
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the call to abandon the Bill, noting the 2023 Act's immunity provisions were opposed by all Northern Ireland parties and victims' groups.

deb_ex.t: We will come to debate that amendment, along with all the other amendments that hon. and right hon. Members have tabled, when we get to the Committee stage. The judgment in the Tho
deb_ex.sum: Defers the specific amendment to Committee stage and reaffirms the long-established principle that national security responsibility rests with Ministers while committing to maximum disclosure.

deb_ex.t: I hope that we will see co-operation in response to the requests that the Independent Commission for Reconciliation and Information Recovery is making of the Irish Government.
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Irish Government's published legislative outline and the Dillon judgment as grounds for expecting fuller Irish co-operation with the commission's information requests.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Gentleman makes a powerful argument for why the troubles Bill should be passed, because it will enable precisely the information sharing with the Irish authorities t
deb_ex.sum: Argues the Bill's information-sharing provisions are precisely the answer to the DUP's concerns and reaffirms that is a central reason to proceed with the legislation.

deb_ex.t: given the recent serious disorder, there is a problem that needs to be tackled.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms he regularly meets the Northern Ireland Executive and PSNI on community cohesion and acknowledges recent serious disorder as a problem requiring action.

deb_ex.t: nurses described to me how, because of the colour of their skin, they were too afraid to leave the hospital at the end of their shift
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the condemnation, shares harrowing accounts from hospital nurses too afraid to leave work due to racist thuggery, and says the events should give cause for deep concern.

deb_ex.t: there is no doubt that part of the violence was fuelled by that kind of online hatred.
deb_ex.sum: Explains that far-right groups used a publicly available Belfast council list to target houses and stresses that social media companies and Ofcom have clear obligations under the Online Safety Act to tackle online hatred that fuelled the vi

deb_ex.t: political leaders have a responsibility to call out what was witnessed for what it is and not mince our words
deb_ex.sum: Sets out shared responsibilities across political leaders, social media companies, police, community organisations and parents for calling out and preventing racist violence in Belfast.

deb_ex.t: there is now another other: the ethnic minority population of Northern Ireland, who are terrified about what is happening.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges Northern Ireland's ongoing post-Good Friday Agreement journey of shared history but differing memory, and warns that ethnic minority communities are now terrified and must not become a new target of division.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is right to raise this issue, because five of the main parties have now come forward with various proposals for reform. I have said to the party leaders that I wish
deb_ex.sum: Confirms willingness to meet party leaders on institutional reform proposals, notes budget pressures are currently absorbing effort, and highlights new PSNI powers to remove paramilitary flags.

deb_ex.t: There is a responsibility, above all, on the Northern Ireland Executive to deliver for the people of Northern Ireland.
deb_ex.sum: Places responsibility on the Northern Ireland Executive to deliver, notes that prolonged Executive absence has hindered progress, and links community stability to resolving the acute housing and water infrastructure crisis.

deb_ex.t: About 1,000 people who had no right to be in Northern Ireland have been removed, including 500 who have been returned to the Republic of Ireland.
deb_ex.sum: Highlights increased operations and arrests, removal of around 1,000 people with no right to be in Northern Ireland, and points to intelligence-led policing under Operation Gull at ports and workplaces.

deb_ex.t: I regularly meet representatives of the logistics sector and businesses trading between Great Britain and Northern Ireland—for instance, through the Northern Ireland business stake
deb_ex.sum: Confirms he regularly meets the logistics sector and businesses to discuss making the Windsor Framework operate as smoothly as possible.

deb_ex.t: if things are as bad as he suggests, why is Northern Ireland one of the fastest-growing parts of the United Kingdom economy?
deb_ex.sum: Defends the carbon charge on ferry routes as protecting Northern Ireland businesses from the carbon border adjustment mechanism, and challenges Wilson's negative characterisation by pointing to Northern Ireland's strong economic growth.

deb_ex.t: I met the leaders of the main Northern Ireland political parties on Thursday 11 June to discuss the terrible disorder. The attack on Mr Ogilvie was truly shocking, but the racist v
deb_ex.sum: Reports meeting Northern Ireland party leaders to discuss the disorder and condemns both the original attack and the racist violence that followed.

deb_ex.t: The single most important thing that we can all do as political leaders is to be absolutely clear that everyone who has made the United Kingdom their home lawfully should be treate
deb_ex.sum: Affirms that everyone lawfully living in the UK deserves equality, respect and dignity regardless of origin, presenting this as the most important message political leaders can send.

deb_ex.t: I am grateful to my hon. Friend for what she says, and I agree with her. There was terrible disorder in Ballymena last year, as a result of which a number of steps were taken to br
deb_ex.sum: Points to Ballymena as an example of community trust-building after disorder, noting it was not repeated there, and calls for more such community work.

deb_ex.t: I hope the hon. Lady will recognise that the common travel area, which is more than a century old, is of great benefit to the citizens of the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ire
deb_ex.sum: Defends the common travel area as beneficial to citizens on both sides of the border, rules out border immigration controls as unrealistic, and cites 1,000 removals since the election including 500 to the Republic.

deb_ex.t: I join the hon. Gentleman in thanking and praising the brave officers of the PSNI. My hon. Friend the Member for Wirral West (Matthew Patrick) and I visited the officers at Strandt
deb_ex.sum: Joins in praising PSNI officers, notes the injuries sustained during the disorder, and promises further discussion on the new training centre.

deb_ex.t: we will do everything we can to protect the norms by which our democracy is felt across the country
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the Government's commitment to protecting democratic norms via the defending democracy taskforce and promises to engage with colleagues on amendments to the Representation of the People Bill.

deb_ex.t: People should exercise caution before they comment on this case—that is the right way to behave for those who wish to see justice done
deb_ex.sum: Calls on everyone to avoid speculation about the case, explains that police are constrained in what they can release, and urges the House to send out a clear message about expectations.

deb_ex.t: I shall discuss this matter with colleagues on a cross-party basis, and I will speak with Mr Speaker and the House authorities
deb_ex.sum: Promises to take up the issue of media publishing home details of Members and former Members in cross-party discussions and with Mr Speaker and the House authorities.

deb_ex.t: we must now live up to our responsibilities to former Members of Parliament as well
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the tribute, affirms the Government's serious duty toward the security of both current and former MPs, and states it must not be the case that serving in the House increases the risk of a violent death.

deb_ex.t: we as a society have to take a stronger position on the right boundary between contested debate and unacceptable behaviour and abuse online
deb_ex.sum: Confirms the Government will work closely with Mr Speaker and the Parliamentary Security Department and stresses the need for society to draw a firmer line between contested debate and unacceptable online behaviour.

deb_ex.t: I will ensure that the House is updated soon after the summer recess
deb_ex.sum: Commits to cross-government discussions, specifically with DSIT, on regulating harmful social media behaviours and promises to update the House after the summer recess.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for that contribution. He will know that colleagues in DSIT are working carefully on the Online Safety Act 2023 and its further implementation, learning less
deb_ex.sum: Points to DSIT's work on implementing the Online Safety Act, commits to cross-government discussion on strengthening the boundary of acceptable online behaviour, and vows to update the House on the programme of work.

deb_ex.t: That was a very moving and funny set of memories from the right hon. Gentleman—very affecting. “Keep calm and carry on” are definitely words to live by, and we could all do with ta
deb_ex.sum: Warmly receives the tribute and memories of Ann Widdecombe and echoes best wishes to the police in their investigation.

deb_ex.t: I urge everyone, wherever they may sit on the political spectrum, to exercise calm and careful judgment before hitting the send button on social media messages
deb_ex.sum: Shares revulsion at denigrating comments about Ann Widdecombe and urges everyone across the political spectrum to pause and reflect before posting on social media.

deb_ex.t: I am sure we will have to go further. As I have committed before, I will make sure the House is updated in due course
deb_ex.sum: Places on record gratitude for counter-terrorism police, agrees with members' points about social media platform unaccountability, and commits to updating the House on further government action.

deb_ex.t: I think the right hon. Lady is absolutely right. When I was first elected in 2010, I used to run an open, first-come-first-served advice surgery, but that is no longer possible, an
deb_ex.sum: Reflects on how her own advice surgeries have had to change since the murders of Jo Cox and Sir David Amess, agrees the connection between MPs and constituents is precious, and affirms the Government's determination to preserve good British

deb_ex.t: any abuse or harassment by Members of Parliament of other Members of Parliament is unacceptable. We should all moderate our language
deb_ex.sum: Urges all Members to moderate their language toward colleagues, states any harassment by MPs of other MPs is unacceptable, confirms no specific threat to Reform UK MPs of which she is aware, and offers the Reform leader a meeting with RAVEC

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Gentleman will know that it is an independent process within the Home Office that deals with the risk assessment and risk management of those in public life. I am no
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's position by emphasising the independent, non-political nature of RAVEC's risk assessments and declines to comment on specific cases, assuring the House that operational independence will be maintained.

deb_ex.t: this country also cannot do without the work of its local councillors, parish councillors and all the people who put in the hours to make their local area better
deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly, acknowledging the risk to local councillors as well as parliamentarians, and confirms the Government is learning lessons from the defending democracy taskforce and Operation Ford with further developments expected.

deb_ex.t: this Government have begun the work of restoring order to our borders. That starts by taking the fight to the criminal gangs.
deb_ex.sum: The Home Secretary moves Second Reading, setting out the chaos inherited from the Conservatives, progress made on enforcement and asylum decisions, and the case for the Bill to restore fairness and control to the asylum system.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for what he said. He is absolutely right: we need to reduce the pressure in local communities as much as possible. He knows that dispersal accommodation has
deb_ex.sum: Agrees dispersal accommodation pressure must fall and argues the best way to achieve that is reducing small boat arrivals, which is the Bill's purpose.

deb_ex.t: around 94,000 people remain in asylum accommodation at a total cost of £3.7 billion per year
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the question about her future role and returns to the scale of the remaining challenge, including 94,000 people in asylum accommodation and continued channel deaths.

deb_ex.t: there is a moral responsibility on all of us to think about how we deal with the particular challenge of small boats crossing the channel
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that channel deaths receive too little attention, argues there is a moral responsibility to stop the trade, and frames the Bill as essential to preserving public consent for asylum.

deb_ex.t: Indefinite leave to remain, and the Government’s proposals on earned settlement, will be settled policy later this year when the Government respond to the earned settlement consult
deb_ex.sum: Says earned settlement policy will be settled later this year following the consultation and notes it is not the subject of the Bill.

deb_ex.t: I remind my hon. Friend that, as he knows, we have paused family reunification, and the Government have said that we will bring forward further proposals for our approach to that.
deb_ex.sum: Reminds her colleague that family reunification is paused and further proposals are coming, and argues the current system lacks coherence and fairness across different migrant categories.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right. When people arrive through controlled, safe routes, when we have made a decision to allow people to enter, and when we are in control and not th
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that controlled, legal routes unlock the British public's generosity and frames community sponsorship as the foundation of the Government's asylum approach.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right—yes, they can and they do. That is the difference with a safe and legal route that has buy-in from communities across the country, and that is th
deb_ex.sum: Agrees community sponsorship schemes work and affirms they will be the basis for the future asylum system.

deb_ex.t: Numbers on those schemes will grow. We will also make it possible for businesses to sponsor refugees to come to this country and provide them with work opportunities.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the new student refugee, community sponsorship and business sponsorship routes opening from autumn, with first arrivals in 2027, and explains how numbers will grow as illegal routes are reduced.

deb_ex.t: it has been settled Government policy to increase the qualifying period from five years to 10 years since last summer—since before I was Home Secretary
deb_ex.sum: Defends settled Government policy on the ILR qualifying period increase and confirms the earned settlement consultation on transitional arrangements will conclude in due course.

deb_ex.t: When we have settled policy later this year, those changes will be subject to the usual procedure for changes to immigration rules
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that the Bill concerns asylum, human rights and appeals only, and that ILR changes will follow the standard immigration rules procedure with full parliamentary scrutiny.

deb_ex.t: I will give way to the right hon. Lady, but I will make progress after that.
deb_ex.sum: Indicates she will take one more intervention before making progress with her speech.

deb_ex.t: I say to the right hon. Lady, for whom I have the greatest respect, that it is not as if I am about to forget my own background, so I do not really need other people to remind me o
deb_ex.sum: Pushes back firmly on Abbott's intervention, notes her own background, and refocuses on breaking the people-smuggling trade by shifting to controlled safe and legal routes.

deb_ex.t: others have been made simply to delay a legitimate removal from this country
deb_ex.sum: Disagrees with critics of the appeals reforms, arguing that non-legally qualified decision makers operate across many tribunals and that the appeals queue is being gamed to delay legitimate removals.

deb_ex.t: A person does not have to be a judge to have good judgment.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the new independent immigration appeals authority staffed by adjudicators rather than judges, arguing this will provide greater capacity and flexibility than the current judicial model.

deb_ex.t: 50% of a 150,000 backlog is still 75,000 cases
deb_ex.sum: Responds that even 50% of a 150,000 backlog is a vast number and defends the single appeal route as targeting behaviours designed to frustrate lawful removal.

deb_ex.t: Our adjudicators will be paid professionals who are trained to make robust, defensible decisions.
deb_ex.sum: Details the new adjudicator structure, including a smaller cohort of legally trained adjudicators and an upper tribunal appeal on points of law, arguing decisions will be robust and defensible.

deb_ex.t: its decisions will be entirely independent of Government, with every Minister of the Crown compelled to uphold the independence of the authority
deb_ex.sum: Insists the new authority will be fully independent of government, with ministers compelled to uphold that independence, and explains the appointment process.

deb_ex.t: I will give way to my hon. Friend who has not asked a question yet.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly invites a colleague who has not yet spoken to put a question.

deb_ex.t: All such appointments will be subject to the usual public appointments principles, which will apply here as they do elsewhere.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms appointments will follow standard public appointments principles and offers to discuss additional safeguards with Members as the Bill progresses.

deb_ex.t: I have given way to my hon. Friend before; I will make progress and come back to him. In the new system, a single, faster appeal route will be established, as addressed in clauses
deb_ex.sum: Explains the single appeal route that requires claimants to raise all matters upfront, with an expedited process for late claims, and introduces the core protection model replacing two overlapping statuses.

deb_ex.t: I will give way to my hon. Friend the Member for Edinburgh East and Musselburgh
deb_ex.sum: Briefly manages contributions from colleagues before taking the next intervention.

deb_ex.t: I think my hon. Friend means mandatory reconsideration in the context of a case when an appeal is made.
deb_ex.sum: Seeks to clarify her colleague's point about mandatory reconsideration in the context of an appeal.

deb_ex.t: before a case proceeds to appeal, we already have an internal process whereby we check whether we should still defend the claim at appeal stage
deb_ex.sum: Explains that an internal checking process already exists before cases proceed to appeal and expresses reluctance to add further bureaucratic layers.

deb_ex.t: he kept putting in appeal after appeal after appeal after appeal. These reforms are designed to deal with that problem.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the need to improve initial decision quality but insists multiple reforms are needed simultaneously, and uses the example of a foreign national offender's repeated appeals to justify the single appeal route.

deb_ex.t: last-minute claims have been made by a convicted rapist, a gangster jailed for possession of a firearm, and an attempted murderer
deb_ex.sum: Details measures strengthening modern slavery protections for children while addressing abuse of the system, including exclusion of those posing public order risks and penalising late disclosures.

deb_ex.t: I will not, because Madam Deputy Speaker wishes me to wind up quickly. In clause 37, we close another significant loophole. As it stands, those whose claims turn out to be unfounde
deb_ex.sum: Concludes the second reading speech by summarising the Bill's aims: fast and fair decisions, genuine refugee protection, closing human rights loopholes, and introducing a contributory repayment principle for asylum support.

deb_ex.t: lawlessness of any kind will never be tolerated, and the Government stand squarely behind the police as they face down criminality and disorder on our streets.
deb_ex.sum: Home Secretary sets out the facts of the A66 crash, tributes to the fallen officers, the IOPC investigation, subsequent arrests, and government funding support for Cleveland police.

deb_ex.t: It was his Government who cut police numbers, not by a few thousand here and there, or a few hundred, but by 20,000 police officers.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's policing record and funding increases, dismisses the shadow Home Secretary's credibility given Conservative cuts of 20,000 officers, and reaffirms support for Cleveland police and condemnation of disorder.

deb_ex.t: I would be very happy to meet my hon. Friend and colleagues from neighbouring constituencies to discuss these matters in more detail.
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the request for a meeting with local MPs, expresses gratitude for officers' bravery, and signals that additional funding and structural police reform will address the long-term resource issues.

deb_ex.t: from the middle of next year there will be a duty on those platforms to act proactively, not just reactively.
deb_ex.sum: Outlines progress implementing the Online Safety Act and signals willingness to go further on social media regulation, confirms mutual aid will continue as needed, and sets out the government's three-tier policing reform plan.

deb_ex.t: reviewing and reforming the police funding formula are absolutely critical to the programme of police reform.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms funding formula reform is integral to the police structural reform programme, criticises previous governments for repeatedly ducking it, and promises an update once the independent review is complete.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman is a local Member, and he is taking the opportunity to ask a question from the Back Benches to reflect his local interest; I pay tribute to him for his response
deb_ex.sum: Assures the hon. Member that the funding formula review will start from first principles, reflecting demand and local need, and that structural reform of police forces will enable flexibility without permanent reliance on mutual aid.

deb_ex.t: the work that we will do on police funding is a very real part of the wider police reform programme.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the personal difficulty for the hon. Member, reaffirms that police funding and structural reform are linked, and commits to meeting local MPs to discuss how reforms will address the full range of policing needs.

deb_ex.t: police officers are human beings; they are still running towards danger, working very long hours and helping people in their local community, but they do need support.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms national police wellbeing support has been activated and will be monitored, agrees fundamental change to the funding formula and force structures is needed, and explains the rationale for moving to a three-tier policing model.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend for raising this matter in his constituency, which faces some of the same issues as we have seen in Cleveland; I see the same in parts of Birmingham as well.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the dangerous driving and social media glorification trend must be tackled, urges the Member to report local examples to platforms and the Home Office, and points to forthcoming Online Safety Act proactive duties.

deb_ex.sum: Sets out government progress on phase one of the midlands rail hub, including Network Rail's appointment of an alliance to design infrastructure and ongoing consultation on Birmingham upgrades.

deb_ex.t: Following the Government’s decision to move forward with the first phase of the midlands rail hub at the spending review last summer, detailed design work has commenced. We are now
deb_ex.sum: Confirms detailed design work has commenced following the spending review decision but cannot give a specific start date, noting new train services should come on line in the 2030s.

deb_ex.t: It is obviously the case that adequate replacement bus services should be available to rail travellers if there is disruption on the line—for example, if engineering works are taki
deb_ex.sum: Agrees adequate replacement bus services must be available during disruption and offers to follow up if the hon. Member writes with more detail, while noting East Midlands Railway is managing the aftermath of the Bedford train crash.

deb_ex.t: Mass transit systems can radically improve local transport in towns and cities across the UK, but plans can often be slowed down by fragmented funding arrangements, difficulties ac
deb_ex.sum: Outlines government action including a new mass transit taskforce, a call for evidence, and devolution of powers to local leaders to speed up delivery.

deb_ex.t: I agree with my hon. Friend, and I suspect the people of Glasgow are at their wits’ end with the approach to that project, having seen it repeatedly promised and deprioritised over
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the criticism of the SNP's repeated failure to deliver the Glasgow airport rail link and reaffirms the Department's commitment to working with the Scottish Government.

deb_ex.t: I know that the Mayor of West Yorkshire, Tracy Brabin, and the Mayor of York and North Yorkshire, David Skaith, work closely together. The hon. Gentleman is right that transport cr
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges cross-boundary transport challenges and points to the 'Better Connected' strategy, expressing confidence that Yorkshire's elected representatives will work together for the best outcomes.

deb_ex.t: Decarbonising transport is vital for our energy security and to make the transport network fit for the future.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's wide-ranging programme to decarbonise transport, covering EVs, charging, active travel, public transport, low-carbon fuels and maritime innovation.

deb_ex.t: procurement for enhanced wi-fi on all GWR long-distance services will start in the second half of this year.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the relevance of wi-fi to modal shift and confirms that procurement for enhanced wi-fi on GWR long-distance services will begin in the second half of the year.

deb_ex.t: I am delighted to hear of the hon. Gentleman’s enthusiasm for decarbonisation. He is right to support the excellent Wrightbus, which manufactures electric buses in Northern Ireland
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes Shannon's enthusiasm and highlights government work with the bus expert manufacturing panel and mayors to support UK electric bus manufacture, including Wrightbus.

deb_ex.t: I look repeatedly at data produced by both the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders and the Department for Transport about purchases of new vehicles. In June, nearly 30% of v
deb_ex.sum: Defends the ZEV mandate, citing rising EV sales and rapid chargepoint roll-out, and insists the government will back the electric transition while keeping the mandate under review.

deb_ex.t: We will not change the 2030 phase-out date for pure internal combustion engine vehicles, and we will not change the 2035 phase-out date for hybrids.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the 2030 and 2035 phase-out dates, blames the previous government for damaging demand by cancelling them, and confirms a ZEV mandate review will be completed within six months.

deb_ex.t: Better, more reliable transport drives good growth, spreads opportunities and makes lives easier. That is our mission, and we are getting on with the job.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's transport achievements: new rail station, public ownership punctuality gains, fare enforcement, free bus travel for children, and a new cycling and walking strategy.

deb_ex.t: I do agree with my hon. Friend. Performance on Avanti West Coast has not been good enough, and I am acutely aware that this part of the network—still privately run—has seen reliabi
deb_ex.sum: Agrees performance on Avanti West Coast has been poor and confirms the route will enter public ownership next year.

deb_ex.t: somebody who is hit by a car travelling at 30 mph is five times more likely to die than someone who is hit by a car travelling at 20 mph.
deb_ex.sum: Defends 20 mph zones on road safety grounds, stressing that decisions rest with local authorities and not central government.

deb_ex.t: I would be happy to ask the Minister for Road Safety to discuss this matter further with my hon. Friend and ensure appropriate meetings take place.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to ask the road safety minister to facilitate appropriate meetings with the hon. Member.

deb_ex.t: I would at least expect them not to work squarely against the interests of local people in the way that my hon. Friend describes.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the MP's legal reading and criticises the Reform-led council for acting against local people's interests, urging it to support the MP's campaign.

deb_ex.t: this is a decision for the Mayor of the West Midlands. I am sure that she will continue to campaign on this issue
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the request for a successor's note and reaffirms that the Aldridge station decision rests with the Mayor of the West Midlands, encouraging the MP to keep campaigning.

deb_ex.t: HS2 will aim to maintain the frequency of services to Scotland, increase the number of available seats for Anglo-Scot journeys and deliver an end-to-end journey experience
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the benefits HS2 will bring to Scotland, including maintained service frequency, more seats and faster end-to-end journeys estimated to be 20 minutes quicker.

deb_ex.t: we are spending £280 million on improving station accessibility during this spending review. I will seek to find new opportunities to fund further work on stations
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the £280 million accessibility spend in this spending review and commits to seeking further funding opportunities through GBR's integrated leadership working with local partners.

deb_ex.t: we need to get maximum benefit for the travelling public. I hope to have future discussions about future rounds of the Access for All scheme
deb_ex.sum: Minister confirms investment in station accessibility through the Access for All scheme, covering 31 stations, and signals future discussions on further rounds.

deb_ex.t: I am very grateful to my hon. Friend and her Committee for their interest in personal safety on the transport network, especially that of women and girls. We have an ambitious, evi
deb_ex.sum: Secretary of State outlines the Government's evidence-based programme to tackle VAWG on the transport network, including nine commitments and funding for CCTV connectivity.

deb_ex.t: I would be happy to meet my hon. Friend to discuss this issue. One of the key things that we are trying to do is improve public transport nodes

deb_ex.t: I make no apology—certainly not to the Opposition—for being able to grab hold of a system that, when we left here in July, was not going to exclude rape offences
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary defends the Government's changing approach as principled improvement, outlines prison capacity additions, foreign national offender removals and the annual reporting commitment, and rejects the Opposition's alternative

deb_ex.t: what surely binds all of us is that we want to reduce reoffending. What I have presented to Parliament today is a measure to get us through a crisis
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary agrees with Abbott on the importance of prison and probation staff and commits to building a new criminal justice system focused on reducing reoffending.

deb_ex.t: I am making a commitment from this Dispatch Box about the quality of engagement with victims and survivors. Everyone is being written to immediately
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary acknowledges the impact on victims, commits to trauma-informed victim liaison engagement, outlines probation investment, and explains his intention to reinvigorate the national Criminal Justice Board.

deb_ex.t: I pay tribute to my hon. Friend for her very direct campaigning to me over the summer about her and her community’s expectations. I join her in what she said about PC Andrew Harper
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary pays tribute to PC Harper and his family, acknowledges the correction of the inequity around emergency worker killings, and commits to working with police to ease pressure on the system.

deb_ex.t: It is part of the conversations that victim liaison officers are having, so that every victim and survivor is able to shape the support around them
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary confirms that victim liaison officers discuss protective support with each victim to ensure they feel safe.

deb_ex.t: I hope they have got the message from the changes in the law that have happened, and the changes that we have now been able to make
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary acknowledges the policing family's scrutiny, expresses hope that the legislative changes signal the Government's commitment, and promises to work with police on long-term system improvement.

deb_ex.t: The right hon. Lady will know of the significant increase in funding to our police that we have already made. Through the National Police Chiefs’ Council, representations have been
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary points to increased police funding already provided and says conversations about additional resourcing through the NPCC are ongoing.

deb_ex.t: I hope that my hon. Friend takes comfort from what both the Prime Minister and I have said about ensuring that the right support is in place for those who are paroled to stay out o
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary commits to ensuring the right support is in place for IPP prisoners to progress through the Parole Board, with public safety as the overriding consideration, and invites ongoing dialogue.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady hits on an important point: what are we using our facilities for if not to rehabilitate people, particularly our young people? That is a symptom of what happens when
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary agrees that rehabilitation, especially for young people, is undermined by an overcrowded estate and says the investment and capacity programme is aimed at creating conditions for proper release preparation.

deb_ex.t: First, I recognise my hon. Friend’s work in the Department, which we are building out from, particularly on the hotline. That is why we have brought it forward. I am pleased that s
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary praises restriction zones as world-leading, commits to maximum engagement with campaigners to ensure they are implemented effectively, and thanks Atkinson for enabling him to highlight them.

deb_ex.t: I will undertake to look at that specific case and get back to her as soon as possible.
deb_ex.sum: The Justice Secretary briefly notes the exclusions already announced and undertakes to look into the specific case Kearns raised and respond as soon as possible.

deb_ex.t: we have taken death by dangerous driving out of scope of the progression model, so anybody whose sentence was being reduced from two thirds to a half
deb_ex.sum: Confirms death by dangerous driving has been removed from the progression model and promises to clarify the release date for the specific case raised.

deb_ex.t: rape has been excluded from the progression model, but I will look at that case as a matter of urgency and come back to him
deb_ex.sum: Confirms rape is excluded from the progression model and promises to look at the specific case urgently, directing the victim to their liaison officer.

deb_ex.t: The answer to that question is no. When the system is running as hot as it is, it becomes a self-defeating cycle
deb_ex.sum: Concedes the current system is not doing enough to prevent reoffending and points to the Prime Minister's housing commitments as grounds for optimism.

deb_ex.t: I hope that there will be a degree of recognition that it was done in the noble cause of wanting to go further, but I still recognise everything he says
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the criticism of victim communications, acknowledges they were sent with good intentions, and commits to ensuring future correspondence is trauma informed.

deb_ex.t: I hope she heard what I said about our enthusiasm for those things that prevent reoffending. The Prisons Minister is looking closely at that in our estate plans
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the government's commitment to rehabilitation provision within prisons and confirms the Prisons Minister is examining estate plans to protect those areas.

deb_ex.t: these sentences have more than had their time—let us work together to bring them to an end
deb_ex.sum: Rejects a binary choice, acknowledges the difficulty of supporting long-term IPP prisoners back into society, and calls for cross-party work to end these sentences.

deb_ex.t: there must always be places for people to go to prison when they have committed serious offences; the worst-case scenario would be either trials collapsing or people being rebailed
deb_ex.sum: Agrees there must always be prison places for serious offenders to prevent trials collapsing or suspects being rebailed into situations where they were offending.

deb_ex.t: court delays are often a factor in the size of the remand population. There is important legislation on that making its way through this House
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the remand population as a significant factor and links its size to court delays, pointing to forthcoming legislation as the vehicle for addressing it.

deb_ex.t: I ask them, as I ask my hon. Friend, to judge us by our actions. We want to get to the same place as them
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the speaker's policing background, asks to be judged by actions, and commits to working with the policing family to ease pressure caused by an overstretched criminal justice system.

deb_ex.t: the MOJ produces a wide range of statistics quarterly, and it will continue to do so. I will, of course, have a look at the important suggestion
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Ministry of Justice's existing quarterly statistics and says he will consider the suggestion, emphasising the public's right to full information.

deb_ex.t: what we are doing to close that gap—is to bring more support forward to ensure that there is direct support, whether through the victims hotline
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the government wanted to go further on exemptions and sets out the support measures, victim hotline and community sector engagement designed to protect survivors.

deb_ex.t: Like pretty much every Lord Chancellor for a number of years now, the first thing in my inbox on day one was a note saying, “By the way, we are going to run out of prison places”—m
deb_ex.sum: Reveals he inherited an imminent capacity crisis on day one, confirms the Sentencing Act has pushed the saturation date back, and commits to a 10-year plan for prison capacity.

deb_ex.t: we are making changes as part of this process. The presumption of tagging eliminates a point of failure, and tagging in prisons—a pilot that is developing—also reduces failure
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the substance of concerns about tagging reliability and outlines improvements including presumption of tagging and prison-tagging pilots, committing to challenge work to demonstrate impact.

deb_ex.t: someone who went to prison for a one-and-a-half-year sentence is still there 18 and a half years later. All of us should feel discomfort about that.
deb_ex.sum: Expresses strong agreement and discomfort at the injustice described, committing to best possible support for IPP prisoners through Parole Board processes and to finding a way to bring IPP to a close.

deb_ex.t: Vetting must be done properly, and my hon. Friend the Prisons Minister and I are working with the Cabinet Office to improve it.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the seriousness of vetting delays and attrition, explains work with the Cabinet Office to improve vetting, and promises to revert directly on the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough question.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend makes a really important point. I think we could say unanimously across this place that if an individual out on licence contacted their victim, that would be a signi
deb_ex.sum: Distinguishes serious licence breaches from more technical non-compliance, defends the principle of attendance at meetings, but agrees to look at the recall system to ensure it is effective.

deb_ex.t: I have been having conversations with my right hon. Friend the Secretary of State for Education very recently on that point.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees fully, citing recent conversations with the Education Secretary and reflecting on his own experience as a local councillor acting as corporate parent to children in care.

deb_ex.t: Deflating it in the ways that I have talked about will help us to build a more stable regime and a better place to work.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges retention and attrition challenges and argues that deflating the prison population will stabilise the regime and make the estate a better place to work.

deb_ex.t: the critical thing is high-quality engagement with victim liaison officers so that those individuals have certainty about what is happening
deb_ex.sum: Points to the victims helpline, funding for local organisations and high-quality victim liaison officer engagement as the key mechanisms to support survivors through early release.

deb_ex.t: We of course want to have effective workload management tools in place. That is what myself and my hon. Friend the Prisons Minister are working closely on
deb_ex.sum: Explains the old system is being replaced because it is 15 years old and outlines ambitions for better technology including AI transcription, pledging effective workload management tools in the new model.

deb_ex.t: That is an excellent suggestion by my right hon. Friend; I will be in touch with Bob. We do not intend for this to be a long, drawn-out process. We want to build from the best evid
deb_ex.sum: Accepts the suggestion enthusiastically, commits to contacting Bob Neill and emphasises that the process will not be drawn out but will build on the best available evidence.

deb_ex.t: I again recognise the impact of the uncertainty across the summer. On the point about victim support, it is about high-quality engagement through victim liaison officers
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the appalling case and the uncertainty victims faced over the summer, and points to victim liaison officers, local support services and augmented funding for the victims helpline as ongoing support.

deb_ex.t: Traditionally, victims and survivors have lived their lives around the licence conditions of their perpetrator. We need to flip that, and restriction zones give us that chance.
deb_ex.sum: Argues restriction zones represent a significant shift by flipping the dynamic so victims no longer have to organise their lives around their perpetrator's licence conditions.

deb_ex.t: I was with staff on Friday and I was tagged, as colleagues may have seen. I have to say it worked very effectively in that case.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges points of failure but highlights improving technology and compliance, and describes personally being tagged to underline the government's commitment to making the system work.

deb_ex.t: I really recognise the importance of that question, and indeed the anxiety caused for survivors of domestic abuse as a result of the changes. We need clearer, earlier flagging. Tha
deb_ex.sum: Norris acknowledges anxiety for domestic abuse survivors and outlines government commitments to earlier flagging, better investment, and improved victim liaison engagement.

deb_ex.t: The provisions under the Modern Slavery Act 2015 drive industry action via due diligence and transparency to tackle forced labour in supply chains for solar panels. All procurement
