we need to do all that we can to strengthen our energy security here at home. The answer is for us to move away from fossil fuels
deb_ex.sum: Minister sets out the government's position that energy security is best achieved by moving away from fossil fuels toward domestically controlled renewables and nuclear.

deb_ex.t: Geothermal has an important part to play and we have to accelerate the potential of all low-carbon energy sources, including geothermal.
deb_ex.sum: Minister welcomes the question on geothermal, affirms it has a role to play in low-carbon heat, and promises to continue looking at planning barriers and heat network infrastructure.

deb_ex.t: He should tell his constituents why he supports a party that is against the new jobs of the future, which would help his constituents
deb_ex.sum: Declines to comment on specific projects but defends the government's approach, arguing oil and gas alone cannot guarantee energy security and accuses the Conservatives of opposing the new offshore wind jobs that would benefit the hon. Memb

deb_ex.t: she continues to peddle nonsense on social media. I think she should look at some of the facts before she does that.
deb_ex.sum: Refuses to retract the scaremongering characterisation, says the shadow Secretary of State should share any evidence with the Department, and insists the grid is robust and met all consumer demand through the heatwave.

deb_ex.t: Ministers commissioned Great British Energy Nuclear’s study of Scotland’s potential for new nuclear last autumn. That study indicates that Scotland has land areas with high potenti
deb_ex.sum: Confirms Great British Energy Nuclear commissioned a study of Scotland's nuclear potential and says the government is open to discussions with the Scottish Government.

deb_ex.t: every single opinion poll a majority of Scots show that they support nuclear energy
deb_ex.sum: Pushes back on the SNP's opposition, citing majority Scottish public support for nuclear, Scotland's existing nuclear baseload, and the jobs lost to Scotland due to SNP policy.

deb_ex.t: because of the out-of-touch ideological approach of the SNP we will not have the opportunity to build those power stations in Scotland
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that over 5,000 Scots work in nuclear but outside Scotland, and blames the SNP's ideological opposition for denying Scotland those jobs and skills.

deb_ex.t: I echo the shadow Minister’s words about those who lost their lives on Piper Alpha 38 years ago. That event was a wake-up call in respect of safety in the industry, but, as the hon
deb_ex.sum: Echoes tribute to Piper Alpha victims, welcomes Conservative support, and commits to pursuing nuclear sites in Scotland while blaming Scottish Government planning regulations for slowing progress.

deb_ex.t: What I love about the shadow Minister is how every single time his face gives away the fact that he does not believe a word he is saying. However, I welcome the former Minister for
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the Conservatives' nuclear record as all talk and no delivery, and sets out the government's own delivery on Hinkley, Sizewell C and small modular reactors.

deb_ex.t: the Government and industry have committed themselves to exploring future research and demonstration opportunities for agrivoltaic systems.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position supporting agrivoltaics through UKRI-funded initiatives and the solar road map, committing to future research and demonstration opportunities.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is absolutely right, and we are in favour of innovation wherever we can deploy solar. He talks about solar on reservoirs, which is absolutely an opportunity that we
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the case for agrivoltaics, highlights support for Lancaster University research and solar-farm visits, and confirms the government wants to go further.

deb_ex.t: even if we hit our most ambitious targets, less than 0.6% of farmland will be taken up with solar.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's approach by stating farming and solar can coexist, noting less than 0.6% of farmland would be used, and expressing hope of finding common ground on rooftop solar.

deb_ex.t: We love community energy and we are determined to see much more of it all across the country. Through the local power plan, which we published recently, we are rolling out the bigg
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's local power plan to expand community energy, promising over 1,000 projects and £1 billion investment through GB Energy by 2030.

deb_ex.t: That sounds like a great project, and I would be happy to meet my hon. Friend, as I would anyone across the House who has exciting community energy projects in their area. The loca
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the constituency project, agrees to meet, and explains that the local power plan addresses both investment and regulation to allow communities to sell power locally.

deb_ex.t: I love all the work that the hon. Member has been doing on community energy; I am tempted to say that we were going to do it anyway, but it was great to have the report on my bedsi
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the committee's work, confirms the government will legislate in the energy independence Bill to let communities sell power and retain profits, and points to the £1 billion GB Energy investment.

deb_ex.t: I love Bellshill, and it was a pleasure to visit the other day to see this fantastic facility opening just across my constituency boundary. More than 300 wind turbines are being ma
deb_ex.sum: Celebrates the Bellshill facility opening, emphasising that the clean energy mission creates skilled local jobs as well as deploying renewables.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Lady could go on all day reading out the things that this Government are already going to do. We want to see much more community ownership, because it matters to us that c
deb_ex.sum: Affirms the Government's commitment to community energy ownership, points to £1 billion of investment, and says the energy independence Bill will remove historic barriers.

deb_ex.t: That does not mean at all that we are not hugely ambitious about solar on car parks.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies the government did not abandon car park solar ambitions but decided against a single mandatory national approach after consultation, while reaffirming strong support for expanding solar on car parks.

deb_ex.t: Yes, I completely agree. I am sure that if my hon. Friend’s local authority is listening, it will hurry up and make those decisions. We also want the process to be more standardise
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the process needs to speed up and says the government wants to standardise permissions across the country so community projects can proceed more quickly.

deb_ex.t: I suspect that in the coming days England fans will learn a lot from Norway in something else. On the serious point that the hon. Member raises, we should first recognise that Norw
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's position by noting Norway's different historic approach and clarifying that the government is not shutting down North Sea production, pointing to transitional energy certificates for new production.

deb_ex.t: First, we are delighted to be building the first long-duration energy storage in Britain in 40 years, including pumped hydro storage projects that will help us store renewable ener
deb_ex.sum: Defends the pumped hydro storage projects as the first long-duration energy storage in 40 years and disputes the claim about jobs, while offering to look further at the community benefits point.

deb_ex.t: the security and resilience of all our energy infrastructure has never been more important
deb_ex.sum: Asserts the Government takes energy resilience seriously, places responsibility on individual developers to comply with regulations, and signals further action may be taken.

deb_ex.t: this is not a Government project so the Government do not have all the details. It is a private project
deb_ex.sum: Shanks defends the Government's record, saying he answered all written questions and explaining that the Peak Cluster project is private and the Government therefore does not hold the detailed data McVey requested.

deb_ex.t: We absolutely need greenhouse gas removal technologies to reach net zero and to tackle the climate crisis.
deb_ex.sum: Welcomes the debate and outlines six government steps to support GGR deployment including the GGR business model contract for difference mechanism, signals the British carbon bank proposal will be considered seriously.

deb_ex.t: On 7 July, the shadow Secretary of State, the right hon. Member for East Surrey (Claire Coutinho), wrote to the Government alleging practices of poor information handling in NESO a
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's response to whistleblower allegations, confirms an independent investigation is under way, and reassures the House that the grid remained stable during the heatwave.

deb_ex.t: it is irresponsible to suggest, in this place and on social media, that our energy system was at risk in recent periods
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's handling of the allegations, argues the shadow Secretary of State is conflating whistleblower concerns with blackout risk, and reaffirms that the grid met demand throughout the heatwave.

deb_ex.t: it is scaremongering to take to social media or come to the House and somehow imply that we were close to blackouts, which is simply not the case
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the committee chair's distinction, reaffirms that the whistleblower allegations will be fully investigated, but repeats that suggesting blackouts were imminent is scaremongering.

deb_ex.t: grid stability is foundational to everything in our energy system. That is why we are investing record amounts in upgrading the grid so that it is resilient for the future
deb_ex.sum: Confirms transparency is central to the inquiry, explains corporate affairs staff do not interfere with operational decisions, and highlights record grid investment including storage.

deb_ex.t: electricity supplies were maintained throughout the June heatwave. No customer demand was subject to disconnection. Statutory frequency limits were maintained throughout the event
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms that electricity supplies were maintained throughout the June heatwave, no customers were disconnected, and statutory frequency limits were never breached.

deb_ex.t: I pay tribute to the right hon. Gentleman, and to all who were involved in that incredibly important exercise. I was not aware of it at all until I came into this job and read the
deb_ex.sum: Confirms awareness of Exercise Mighty Oak, notes most actions are now completed, and outlines ongoing cross-government resilience exercises to keep preparedness current.

deb_ex.t: our aim as a House should surely be to do everything we can to prevent that extreme weather from becoming even more frequent
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that margin notices are standard tools, confirms no customers were disconnected, and urges rebuilding consensus on tackling extreme weather through clean energy policy.

deb_ex.t: at no time did we not meet demand across the country, and at no time were we close to disconnecting anyone whatsoever from the system
deb_ex.sum: Rejects accusations of complacency, condemns talk of blackouts as irresponsible, and reiterates that demand was met on every day in question while the investigation will address the serious allegations.

deb_ex.t: we are driving forward the biggest upgrade in the grid in generations, and the work that the operators do at NESO is a critical part of that
deb_ex.sum: Argues the previous government failed to invest sufficiently in the grid and that the current government is driving the biggest grid upgrade in generations to handle increasingly complex demands.

deb_ex.t: I am not seeking in any way to suggest that we should not be transparent, but I am suggesting that we need to let the inquiry run its course
deb_ex.sum: Confirms engagement with NESO governance structures, declines to pre-empt the inquiry on document handling, and commits to transparency while urging the House to await the inquiry's findings.

deb_ex.t: We are quite an outlier in Europe in not engaging with the public regularly on the question of personal and household resilience
deb_ex.sum: Agrees on the need for public resilience communication, commits to greater household preparedness engagement across government, and promises the inquiry report will be published and shared with the House.

deb_ex.t: I think we are probably speaking at cross-purposes. I suspect that when the shadow Secretary of State refers to blackouts, she means a national power outage rather than supply disr
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies the distinction between national blackouts and local supply disruptions, and offers to follow up personally on the recurring issue in Tunbridge Wells.

deb_ex.t: I congratulate my hon. Friend on getting a question about nuclear into this, and she is absolutely right.
deb_ex.sum: Briefly affirms his hon. Friend's point about nuclear energy's importance with light-hearted acknowledgement.

deb_ex.t: Nuclear is going to play a really critical part in our future energy needs. It provides the stable baseload power that runs on the system 24/7 for decades.
deb_ex.sum: Strongly endorses nuclear as critical baseload power and sets out the Government's commitments including Sizewell C, Hinkley, small modular reactors and Fingleton review reforms.

deb_ex.t: if we had not built renewables without strategically planning where they were and the grid to connect them into, we would not be paying that money.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's energy mix strategy including nuclear and storage, and rejects the Conservative argument against grid investment, pointing out that inadequate strategic planning under the previous Government caused constraint payme

deb_ex.t: I almost thought my hon. Friend had asked a question without mentioning Harlow, but we got there in the end. I am afraid I cannot give him a specific answer about the work we are d
deb_ex.sum: Outlines the Government's two-pronged approach of large-scale grid investment and reforming the connections queue to deliver clean, affordable power to constituents including those in Harlow.

deb_ex.t: It has been asked to carry out an independent review. The findings will be reported to the independent director on the NESO board, and it will be shared with Ofgem.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the independence of the Eversheds Sutherland review, explains the reporting structure to the independent NESO board director and Ofgem, and notes the Government has not yet seen the full whistleblower allegations.

deb_ex.t: whistleblowers are protected under legislation, and rightly so. That is important, and we have reiterated to all those involved in this incident that they are protected in law
deb_ex.sum: Confirms existing legal protections for whistleblowers and explains how the inquiry process will allow them to give evidence without management present, while deferring the office of the whistleblower proposal to other Ministers.

deb_ex.t: a significant part of the issue was caused by gas power stations not being able to operate at full capacity because of the heat.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the need for gas as a silver bullet, noting alternative tools exist for inertia and pointing out that gas stations themselves struggled during the heatwave.

deb_ex.t: An independent inquiry will now interview them to establish the facts. We should wait for those facts before we jump to conclusions.
deb_ex.sum: Pushes back on the characterisation that he dismissed Tunbridge Wells blackouts, reiterates his offer to investigate, and defends the inquiry process as properly independent and evidence-based.

deb_ex.t: investment is necessary to bring down the costs in the long term. We are currently paying to constrain the renewables that are generating often much more electricity day after day
deb_ex.sum: Explains that upfront grid investment is necessary to reduce long-term constraint costs and deliver cheap renewable power, blaming the previous Government for building renewables without connecting them.

deb_ex.t: Data centres are an opportunity to soak up some of what we are currently constraining, which will actually bring down bills. If we can deploy them in the right places
deb_ex.sum: Outlines how data centres can help absorb constrained electricity and reduce bills, describes the cross-departmental data centre strategy, and commits to ensuring communities benefit from AI infrastructure.

deb_ex.t: I am disappointed, Madam Deputy Speaker. I heard that the hon. Gentleman rapped some of his speech in a Westminster Hall debate today, so I am disappointed that he did not do a rap
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the transferred nature of Northern Ireland's grid while affirming the importance of interconnectors with Ireland and Northern Ireland for system balancing and commits to taking the points away.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Gentleman and I have had this discussion before. This is a very, very important point: of course, we have to do more on adaptation, but the idea that we give up on tacklin
deb_ex.sum: Rejects the suggestion of abandoning mitigation, arguing that allowing temperatures to rise to 3.5–4° would be grossly irresponsible economically and for the population, and insists the government must do both adaptation and mitigation.

deb_ex.t: Well, that is obviously a matter for discussion across Government, but the hon. Gentleman makes a really important point, and I do agree with it. The May 2026 report of the Climate
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the thrust of the question, acknowledging adaptation has been neglected and that the Climate Change Committee's report is a landmark, while committing to give it greater priority across government.

deb_ex.t: I support all efforts to make people aware of this emergency. Indeed, the state of climate and nature annual statement, which we pioneered last year, will be happening again in the
deb_ex.sum: Expresses support for raising public awareness of the climate emergency, pointing to the government's annual state of climate and nature statement, and argues that people must be shown both the danger and that action is possible.

deb_ex.t: I am proud that we have consented nearly 6 GW of solar power since this Government came into office—around six times the amount that the previous Government consented.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's solar expansion record, citing nearly 6 GW consented and record generation, and links new solar to lower energy bills.

deb_ex.t: No, we are not going to pause our development of solar power—it is essential to get bills down for families and get us off the rollercoaster of fossil fuels.
deb_ex.sum: Rejects calls for a pause on solar development, insists safety is taken seriously and that the Energy Minister is actively working with the National Fire Chiefs Council.

deb_ex.t: I agree with my hon. Friend. He puts it very well. Our renewables auctions have resulted in enough power to power the equivalent of 23 million homes. That is significantly cheaper
deb_ex.sum: Defends renewables auctions as powering 23 million homes at cheaper cost than gas, and contrasts the government's approach with the shadow Secretary of State's preference for gas.

deb_ex.t: What is he on, Mr Speaker? To be clear, even in the most ambitious scenarios, our plans for solar in 2030 would use 0.6% of agricultural land; I am happy to repeat that. I do not k
deb_ex.sum: Dismisses the shadow Minister's land figures as fabricated, defends solar as the cheapest power source, and accuses Conservatives of wanting to keep the country dependent on fossil fuels.

deb_ex.t: In the two years since July 2024, this Government have secured renewable power for the equivalent of 23 million homes, invested in the biggest nuclear building programme in half a
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the Government's two-year record on clean energy, warm homes investment, bill reductions and climate leadership.

deb_ex.t: I appreciate the hon. Gentleman’s question, because the situation facing families who use heating oil has been significant since the Iran war started. That is why we made money ava
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges difficulties for heating-oil households, cites emergency support and boiler upgrade scheme funding, and commits to further discussions.

deb_ex.t: We do look at cumulative impact in the planning process, and the strategic spatial energy plan will be very important.
deb_ex.sum: Commits to examining the suggestion, noting cumulative impact is already considered in planning and that the strategic spatial energy plan will help.

deb_ex.t: This Government have delivered the biggest investment in warm homes in our history, broken records on renewables, and secured over £100 billion of private sector investment.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the Government's two-year record on warm homes, renewables, nuclear and clean energy jobs, contrasting it with the Opposition's legacy.

deb_ex.t: The truth is that we all face a choice on the future of our energy system. Do we learn the lessons of history—of two fossil-fuel crises in five years, as a result of Russia’s invas
deb_ex.sum: Frames the Government's clean energy drive as the necessary lesson from two fossil-fuel crises, arguing for energy sovereignty over continued fossil-fuel dependence.

deb_ex.t: We want to see the opportunities around SMRs throughout the United Kingdom. I am happy to discuss that with him.
deb_ex.sum: Gives an undertaking to consult devolved administrations on SMRs and expresses a desire to share opportunities across the UK.

deb_ex.t: The way to get bills down is to drive for clean energy, which the Conservatives oppose.
deb_ex.sum: Argues that clean energy is the route to lower bills and attributes recent rises to the Iran war, defending the Government's strategy against Conservative opposition.

deb_ex.t: I am sure that there is more to do on brokers. We will look at his suggestions.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the concern about business energy treatment and broker regulation, and commits to examining the suggestions.

deb_ex.t: I can honestly say to him that we have massive enthusiasm from a whole range of private sector companies, and we are driving that forward at pace.
deb_ex.sum: Points to advanced modular reactors and other routes to market, highlighting strong private sector enthusiasm and the government's commitment to driving nuclear forward at pace.

deb_ex.t: That is why we have the £100 billion of private investment. We are going to carry on doing it.
deb_ex.sum: Points to the Clean Power 2030 action plan and £100 billion of private investment as the framework driving jobs and growth in renewables.

deb_ex.t: We think the contracts for difference model is a good one. We want to get on with opening the auction, and we continue to look at all these issues.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the existing contracts for difference model as a good one and says the government will press ahead with the next auction while continuing to keep all options under review.

deb_ex.t: We are an energy policy and industrial policy Department. We have made progress on that and are determined to make further progress.
deb_ex.sum: Affirms that combining energy and industrial policy is central to the department's work and that the government is making and will continue to make progress on British jobs and supply chains.

deb_ex.t: We love Cornwall; we love the potential of what it can provide in terms of floating wind. My hon. Friend states her case incredibly well.
deb_ex.sum: Warmly endorses the potential of floating wind in Cornwall and supports the case made by his colleague.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend makes an incredibly important point. We will write to her with a good answer.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees the point raised is important and undertakes to provide a written answer.

deb_ex.t: This Government will not acquiesce in the destruction of the two-state solution—we will act. I will set out a comprehensive set of measures in the coming weeks.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's condemnation of illegal settlements and settler terrorism, and promises a comprehensive set of measures in the coming weeks.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that broader economic tools including services must be examined and states the government does not want British companies financing or constructing new settlements, with more detail to follow.

deb_ex.sum: Defends the previous government's record on Palestinian state recognition and arms licences, but acknowledges the need for a step change in approach and promises further announcements soon.

deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the legitimate concern about influence but argues that listening to the Palestinian Authority, who say the time to act is now, must weigh heavily in the government's decisions.

deb_ex.sum: Cites record summer heat as evidence that climate change is one of the biggest national security threats and pledges to treat it with appropriate seriousness as Foreign Secretary.

deb_ex.sum: Praises Cornwall's initiative and commits to examining international collaborations including with state governments, framing climate as a collective action problem.

deb_ex.sum: Agrees that aid spending must be value for money and argues it is in Britain's own national interest to address global problems, seeking cross-party agreement on that principle.

deb_ex.sum: Asserts he takes the cost of living crisis seriously and says his priority is working to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to restore oil and gas flows.

deb_ex.t: Baroness Hayman in the other place has visited the port to understand the issues that he describes. We take these issues extremely seriously.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the border biosecurity concerns raised, notes a ministerial visit to the port, and offers to meet the shadow Minister to discuss the issues further.

deb_ex.t: The Government secured a major increase in the UK’s annual bluefin tuna quota from 63 tonnes to around 230 tonnes, creating new opportunities for fishers across the United Kingdom.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's position: a major quota increase was secured and licences were allocated through a fair, transparent ballot process, with ongoing work with devolved governments.

deb_ex.t: As my hon. Friend rightly says, one Scottish fisher secured a commercial bluefin tuna licence in 2025, authorised through a fair and transparent application process. That fisher wa
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the Scottish fisher's unsuccessful 2026 application, explains licences are issued year by year due to demand, and commits to considering the hon. Member's ideas while working with Scottish fisheries administrations.

deb_ex.t: I thank him for his invitation to engage in these issues and I am happy to follow up with him.
deb_ex.sum: Responds warmly to the hon. Member's invitation, references a previous Westminster Hall debate, and commits to following up on Northern Ireland fisheries issues.

deb_ex.t: I take those issues seriously and I want to ensure that there is certainty and clarity in the sector.
deb_ex.sum: Confirms an upcoming meeting with the National Pig Association, notes the farming road map provides certainty, and offers to follow up on the concerns about independent pig producers.

deb_ex.t: We want people to know where their food comes from, trust what they are buying, and back British farmers who meet our high standards.
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the principle of clearer food origin labelling for consumers and farmers and offers to meet the MP to discuss his proposals.

deb_ex.t: I take these issues extremely seriously, and will bring forward the meeting so that I see the organisation as soon as possible.
deb_ex.sum: Thanks the committee chair and commits to bringing forward a meeting with the National Pig Association as soon as possible.

deb_ex.t: I welcome the leadership that my hon. Friend is demonstrating through the APPG on fisheries for industry and coastal communities like ours. The Government are focused on delivering
deb_ex.sum: Praises the MP's APPG leadership and outlines government support measures for the fisheries sector, committing to further engagement with the APPG on its priorities.

deb_ex.t: Vaccination remains the most effective and viable short and long-term control measure against bluetongue, both for this season and in the future.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the government's response to the bluetongue outbreak, covering confirmed cases, testing, vaccination supply and farmer support communications.

deb_ex.t: I stress that vaccination remains the only effective long-term option for disease control, and we will continue to work with keepers of susceptible animals to discuss vaccine optio
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's record on vaccination supply, testing capacity increases and farmer engagement, promising continued work with industry bodies.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend, who is a real champion for the farming community in his constituency. He recently met more than 100 farmers across his patch, and I look forward to working
deb_ex.sum: Praises the hon. Member's farming advocacy and points to the government's 25-year farming road map as the vehicle for building long-term resilience.

deb_ex.t: We are reviewing our processes to help expedite the confirmation of disease and we are considering what further support may be made available to farmers in the future.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the challenges faced by south-west farmers, stresses the importance of vaccination, notes increased testing capacity at Pirbright and says further farmer support is under consideration.

deb_ex.t: As I mentioned earlier, we have increased capacity at the Pirbright Institute and are working closely with the APHA on capacity issues. I am very happy to write to my hon. Friend o
deb_ex.sum: Confirms increased capacity at Pirbright and APHA and offers to write to the hon. Member with specific details.

deb_ex.t: I thank the Chair of the Select Committee for his contribution. He is absolutely right that this is a serious issue that needs serious consideration. I mentioned that DEFRA has tri
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges lessons can always be learned, commits to reviewing NAO findings and Select Committee recommendations, and points to existing communication efforts including webinars and NFU engagement.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend is a real champion on farming issues and I look forward to visiting his constituency in due course to understand the challenges and opportunities farmers there are f
deb_ex.sum: Commits to visiting the hon. Member's constituency, highlights regular engagement with the livestock sector and expresses willingness to hear further concerns from Staffordshire farmers.

deb_ex.t: I do not want to steal the thunder of the Justice Secretary, but he will soon announce a much-enhanced licensing and tagging regime in which victims will be able to be given a say
deb_ex.sum: Burnham previews an enhanced licensing and tagging regime with victim input and restriction zones that he says shifts the balance firmly in favour of victims.

deb_ex.t: We will certainly look at that scheme, and indeed we are doing so. I have been in touch with the Canadian Prime Minister. There are other schemes in Europe. We need to be pragmatic
deb_ex.sum: Burnham confirms the government is actively looking at the scheme and other European collaboration options to meet defence commitments pragmatically.

deb_ex.t: I certainly have not in any way disrespected Scotland. I came to Scotland to support the opening of the Commonwealth games in my first week in office. I met the First Minister. He
deb_ex.sum: Burnham rejects the charge of disrespect, citing his early engagement with Scotland and the First Minister, and argues public support does not currently show a consistent demand for another referendum.

deb_ex.t: It was brilliant to be at Alstom with my hon. Friend and to see all the apprentices that it employs, as well as those employed in its supply chain. It is a model for what we want t
deb_ex.sum: Burnham recalls visiting Alstom with the MP, praises it as a model, and commits to making a massive change on apprenticeships as part of the Milburn report response.

deb_ex.t: The hon. Member has worked hard at that question. Full marks for creativity. It must have looked great in front of the mirror, and it was still pretty good in the House. On the tri
deb_ex.sum: Burnham deflects Cooper's critique with humour, defends the triple-helix model by pointing to Greater Manchester's sustained growth record under it, and suggests Cooper consult Baroness May.

deb_ex.t: That type of connectivity is crucial to local communities, and I completely agree with my hon. Friend.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees that local connectivity is crucial and points to No. 10 North as the vehicle for getting infrastructure back into communities.

deb_ex.t: I have already got Members on the other side of the House championing my achievements as Mayor of Greater Manchester.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the point about the Greater Manchester model and welcomes cross-bench support for his mayoral record.

deb_ex.t: We are serious about making sure that where there are world-class sectors in our communities, we back them properly
deb_ex.sum: Expresses sympathy over Denby Pottery and commits to backing world-class sectors and helping communities transition to future technologies.

deb_ex.t: Bring me a proposal—that is what I say to him. I will look seriously at it
deb_ex.sum: Backs the member's call for public control of ferry prices, draws a parallel with bus fare reductions in Greater Manchester, and invites a formal proposal.

deb_ex.t: Every person in my view is capable of recovery. We just need to give them the circumstances in which it can happen.
deb_ex.sum: Affirms that tackling rough sleeping is about a journey of recovery, not just housing, and expresses belief that every person is capable of recovery given the right support.

deb_ex.t: The climate commitments in our manifesto are not at risk. I have made clear today that we need to plan for a carbon-neutral future.
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's climate commitments as secure and argues for a pragmatic rather than ideological approach to the energy transition.

deb_ex.t: This is a very serious matter indeed, and I believe that news has broken about it as we have been gathering a statement from the German Government about the incident at Leipzig. I
deb_ex.sum: Condemns the Leipzig attack in the strongest terms, affirms full UK solidarity with Germany, and pledges steadfast cooperation with NATO allies against Russian aggression.

deb_ex.t: I happen to agree with the hon. Gentleman. I know that there have been moves to improve the regulation of bailiffs, but I would encourage the 10 councils in Greater Manchester to t
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the member's concerns about bailiff use and debt, noting its destructive effect on mental health, and endorses a different and better approach to debt collection.

deb_ex.t: The model of devolution in England is working, and I want it to be available to all areas.
deb_ex.sum: Points to faster growth in Greater Manchester and Liverpool as proof that devolution works and invites the member to bring a delegation to No. 10 North.

deb_ex.t: I will always respond to a change when it is brought to me with a clear consensus and cross-party support.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the London boroughs' position but notes the complexity of the GLA settlement and says he would look at any proposal brought with genuine cross-party consensus.

deb_ex.t: if we do reindustrialise, the money that we put forward to support that process can pay us back over many years to come
deb_ex.sum: Highlights the potential for sustainable aviation fuel production at Grangemouth and signals willingness to support reindustrialisation investment as a long-term economic return.

deb_ex.t: We will work hard to ensure that the trust of all communities—but particularly the communities that the hon. Lady represents—in the commission is restored.
deb_ex.sum: Clarifies that an independent review of the Parades Commission has been announced and commits to restoring trust in the commission among all communities.

deb_ex.t: there is a need for a resolution on what will happen from Handsacre to Manchester via Crewe, and a solution for the communities in between
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the need for resolution on the HS2 route from Handsacre to Manchester but stops short of committing to a specific outcome, drawing on his own experience.

deb_ex.t: I will ask the Education Secretary to look at precisely the issue that the hon. Lady has raised.
deb_ex.sum: Commits to asking the Education Secretary to examine the per-student funding issue raised for West Sussex.

deb_ex.t: we will not have a health and care system that is fit for the 21st century until it supports people with dementia as well as it treats people with cancer
deb_ex.sum: Agrees with the principle that dementia care should be supported as well as cancer care, while acknowledging the goal has not yet been achieved.

deb_ex.t: I am aware of the concern, and it is similar to the issue that was raised by the hon. Member for Mid Buckinghamshire (Greg Smith). All I can say is that I give the hon. Member for
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges local concern about the asylum centre planning application and promises to review the details and report back.

deb_ex.t: All parts of the UK need to have control over basic services, and I look forward to working with my hon. Friend to support what he is saying.
deb_ex.sum: Endorses the community energy devolution agenda and pledges to work with the MP to advance it across the UK.

deb_ex.t: I remember well visiting Musgrove Park in my days as a Health Minister. I did some work shadowing at the hospital, so I know how much it is in need of renovation. I will look into
deb_ex.sum: Recalls personal knowledge of Musgrove Park's poor condition, acknowledges the pressures on NHS staff and patients, and commits to looking into the current status of the maternity unit.

deb_ex.t: The loaning of the tapestry is a great example of French-British co-operation—the same co-operation that has helped us reduce summer small boat crossings to a seven-year low.
deb_ex.sum: Sets out the day's engagements, highlighting the Bayeux tapestry event as an example of French-British co-operation and noting a seven-year low in small boat crossings.

deb_ex.t: Can I start by paying tribute to the hon. Lady for the way in which she has represented the Jones family? I understand their anguish, and that of the many other families who found
deb_ex.sum: Pays tribute to the MP, acknowledges family anguish, and explains how he pushed for further exclusions including death by dangerous driving, expressing confidence the right position has been reached.

deb_ex.t: May I start by paying tribute to my right hon. Friend for everything she has done to stand up for her constituents, but more so for Wales, particularly in her role as Secretary of
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the extra pressures on capital cities and commits to engaging with the MP on the funding formula review, while noting South Wales police have already received a funding boost.

deb_ex.t: I do not want to be a Prime Minister who sees a situation where we have so many people in their 20s not in education, employment or training.
deb_ex.sum: Deflects the challenge by emphasising the need to reduce welfare dependency among young people and invites cross-party problem solving rather than point scoring.

deb_ex.t: This Government are lowering the cost of living and lowering the cost of business, and that is what we will continue to do.
deb_ex.sum: Claims tax cuts on electricity bills and business rates as his government's fiscal moves and says commitments are fully funded, citing the reallocation of digital ID money.

deb_ex.t: I say to the right hon. Lady that I have worked with Jim O’Neill for 10 years. Jim O’Neill always gives me candid advice. We do not always agree, but he and I worked together to tu
deb_ex.sum: Defends the government's economic record, citing fastest G7 growth in the first half of the year and falling borrowing, and blames market turbulence on the debt exposure left by the previous government.

deb_ex.t: I say to the right hon. Lady that I have already indicated that my first moves were to cut tax, but like any Prime Minister, I am not going to write the Budget here. That will be a
deb_ex.sum: Refuses to pre-empt the Budget on tax, points to the early Budget date as evidence of fiscal seriousness, and attacks the Opposition for defending the Truss mini-Budget that spiked borrowing costs.

deb_ex.t: May I say to the right hon. Lady something I said earlier? Debt was rising as a percentage of GDP under the Government that she, and her new shadow Chancellor, served in. He was ha
deb_ex.sum: Blames the previous government for rising debt as a share of GDP and the mortgage spike on Budget day, and commits to fiscal rules and reducing cost of living pressure.

deb_ex.t: I will start with the serious point made by the right hon. Lady, which is the announcement by the German Government yesterday in relation to the attack in Leipzig. That should unit
deb_ex.sum: Condemns Russia's Leipzig attack, reaffirms solidarity with Germany and Ukraine, and states the government will fully fund the defence investment plan and meet NATO commitments by 2035.

deb_ex.t: I thank my hon. Friend and pay tribute to his campaign on this issue. I was talking about getting an innovation-led economy going in all parts of the country, and that applies to r
deb_ex.sum: Praises the campaign, commits to examining the amendments, and promises a Health Minister meeting, while insisting any changes must be evidence-based and maintain safeguards.

deb_ex.t: I thank the right hon. Gentleman. He is absolutely right to share the analysis that I laid out yesterday. It is clear that the decade of low growth that we have had has been partly
deb_ex.sum: Agrees Brexit contributed to low growth, expresses a desire for a closer EU relationship, and signals priority issues of steel and farming ahead of the upcoming UK-EU summit.

deb_ex.t: I will certainly give a direct answer: I will commit to reopening it but not within days; I am not in a position to make that commitment today. But I am again in agreement with the
deb_ex.sum: Commits to reopening the unit but cannot promise days, acknowledges structural midwife shortages across the UK, and confirms the Health Secretary is reviewing the issue following recent maternity reviews.

deb_ex.t: We certainly will do that. I am in no doubt over the importance of good transport connectivity to young people’s life chances, and I will ask No. 10 North to make contact with my h
deb_ex.sum: Commits to improving transport connectivity for young people and outlines education reforms creating a technical pathway from age 14, criticising the Gove-era education system.

deb_ex.t: Our first responsibility is to get Stormont government up and running and functioning properly with a budget
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to work with the Alliance MP but says the immediate priority is getting Stormont functioning with a budget before tackling broader reform.

deb_ex.t: the big cities of England—I am talking about Leeds and about Bristol—should have mass transit systems
deb_ex.sum: Praises the new stations and commits to working with the Mayor of the West of England to develop a mass transit system connecting Bristol and its wider area.

deb_ex.t: I always took a brownfield-first approach, and that is what I will do
deb_ex.sum: Defends a brownfield-first approach while acknowledging the need for balance, and offers a meeting with the Housing Minister rather than the PM personally.

deb_ex.t: I think there is a case for going further on fireworks and regulating them. On antisocial behaviour more broadly, I supported Greater Manchester police in taking the toughest possible approach
deb_ex.sum: Supports tougher neighbourhood policing, references Operation Vulcan in Greater Manchester, and indicates willingness to go further on fireworks regulation.

deb_ex.t: where proposals come from the Senedd Government, we will give them fair consideration
deb_ex.sum: Says proposals from the Senedd will get fair consideration and expresses willingness to work with Plaid Cymru on growth and devolution, citing the Port Talbot discussions.

deb_ex.t: I have made that commitment, I have made it very clearly, and I have done so for a considerable time. I was in Ukraine last week for a very specific reason: to repeat it on the wor
deb_ex.sum: Reaffirms the commitment to 3% of GDP on defence and links it to reindustrialising British communities and maintaining sovereign manufacturing capability.

deb_ex.t: I will agree here and now to a meeting with him and all Cornish MPs to discuss what we might do, alongside his Bill
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the MP and all Cornish MPs to explore combining his private Member's Bill with devolution deal levers to address second-home issues in Cornwall.

deb_ex.t: We want the maximum number of kids to have access and to stand in front of that tapestry while it is here in the UK
deb_ex.sum: Commits to pressing the British Museum for maximum access for children and praises the MP's campaign, expressing hope that all children can see the tapestry.

deb_ex.t: I indicated that earlier today. Young people who can work should be working. I believe they want to work; the question is whether we have always given them the support they need. A
deb_ex.sum: Defends his Greater Manchester record on NEETs and T-levels, reaffirms that young people who can work should work, and calls for cross-party support.

deb_ex.t: we committed in the summer to community-based mental health provision: to make it easier for people to access that provision
deb_ex.sum: Points to the government's commitment to community-based mental health provision and promises to work with the Health Secretary to address Bedford's specific concerns.

deb_ex.t: No borrowing to fund day-to-day spending, debt falling as a percentage of GDP by the end of the Parliament, and yes, we will
deb_ex.sum: Tersely restates the two fiscal rules and confirms the government will stick to them.

deb_ex.t: I am going to call a wildfire summit, which he will be welcome to attend. Our fire and rescue services are not set up properly for the changing climate.
deb_ex.sum: Acknowledges the wildfire problem and announces a wildfire summit, noting fire and rescue services lack modern equipment and aerial support for the changing climate.

deb_ex.t: I intend to visit Scotland soon to look in detail at the issues in the Aberdeen community, because I know that people have struggled with the impact of transition.
deb_ex.sum: Backs industrial transition for Scotland, promises to visit Aberdeen, and expresses willingness to work with the SNP member on ScotWind and Grangemouth.

deb_ex.t: My hon. Friend has been raising important issues that others have not spoken about—and it is clear to me that her summer was more exciting than mine.
deb_ex.sum: Agrees to meet the hon. Member and praises her for raising important issues, adding a lighthearted joke about her summer being more exciting than his.

deb_ex.t: Can the Minister confirm whether there have been conversations with European counterparts about applying that flexibility at Dover, Folkestone and St Pancras this summer?
deb_ex.sum: Notes the European Commission's provision allowing member states to partially suspend EES checks at peak times, and asks whether flexibility has been discussed for Dover, Folkestone and St Pancras this summer.
